Problem 1

A ball of mass $m=1\ \mathrm{kg}$ attached to an ideal spring of stiffness $k=50\ \mathrm{N/m}$ oscillates in a viscous medium. Figs. 1 and 2 (see the reverse side) show the graphs of velocity versus coordinate and of acceleration versus velocity corresponding to the motion of the ball (the origin of coordinates is chosen at its equilibrium position). Draw the graph of the viscous friction force acting on the ball versus its velocity.

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

A uniform ring of mass $M$ with a small bead of mass $m$ threaded on it lies on a horizontal table. At the initial moment the bead has velocity $v$ and the ring is at rest. Determine the minimum value of the kinetic energy of the bead during the subsequent motion. There is no friction.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

You have at your disposal a source of sinusoidal voltage with amplitude $U$, connecting wires and an ideal transformer with two windings, the ratio of the numbers of turns of which is $1:3$. Find the voltage amplitudes that can be obtained with this equipment.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

An observer located indoors at a distance $L=3\ \mathrm{m}$ from a window covered on the outside by many small water droplets sees on it a bright spot of radius $r=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ from a very distant lamp located at the same level as the observer. Determine the maximum angle that the surface of the droplets makes with the surface of the glass. The refractive index of water is $n=4/3$. Diffraction of light on the droplets is to be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 5
problems.problem:
Problem 5

Natural uranium consists of $n_1=0.7\%$ of the isotope $^{235}\mathrm{U}$ and of $n_2=99.3\%$ of $^{238}\mathrm{U}$. According to modern views, all elements heavier than iron were formed in supernova explosions, and afterwards the planets, in particular, were formed from the resulting gas and dust clouds. Apparently, in these ejecta there were approximately equal amounts of all the isotopes of uranium. Estimate how many years ago the ejection of matter from which our Earth was formed took place. The half-life, i.e. the time during which the number of atoms of a given isotope decreases by a factor of 2, is $T_1=7\cdot10^{8}$ years for $^{235}\mathrm{U}$ and $T_2=4.5\cdot10^{9}$ years for $^{238}\mathrm{U}$.

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

A rhombus is made of rigid rods of length $L$. The rods are fastened at their ends by hinges. At the initial moment two opposite hinges are next to each other (very close) and have zero velocities. One of these hinges is fixed. The other one is set in motion with constant acceleration. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the remaining hinges of the rhombus at the moment when the rhombus becomes a square, if all the rods move remaining in one plane.

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

A tube of length $L$ with a constant internal cross-section in the form of a circle of radius $R$ ($R\ll L$) is bent into a ring. The ring is stationary and its axis is horizontal. An inviscid liquid, whose volume is $V<\pi R^{2}L$, is poured into the tube. What is the period of small oscillations of the liquid near the equilibrium position? The acceleration of free fall is $g$.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

A gas with molar mass $m=60\ \mathrm{g/mol}$ is in a sealed vessel with rigid walls and is maintained at a constant temperature $T=0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The cross-sectional area $S$ of the molecules, which can be treated as hard spheres, is $10^{-19}\ \mathrm{m^2}$. The gas pressure at the beginning of the experiment is $P_0=100\ \mathrm{Pa}$. When the gas is illuminated by ultraviolet light, the molecules that have absorbed a quantum of light go over into an excited state. The mean lifetime of a molecule in the excited state is $t=10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s}$. When two excited molecules collide in the gas, a chemical reaction takes place, as a result of which one new molecule is formed from them. It is known that in 1 second in each cubic centimetre of the gas $N=10^{12}$ molecules are excited. Estimate in what time the pressure in the vessel will decrease by $\varepsilon=1\%$ of the initial one.

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

A racing car has drive on all four wheels. Its engine delivers the maximum power $P=60\ \mathrm{kW}$ at any speed. Neglecting air resistance, calculate the time of acceleration of this car from the start to the speed $v=20\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The mass of the car is $m=1\ \mathrm{t}$, the coefficient of friction between the wheels and the road surface does not depend on the speed and equals $\mu=0.6$.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

A hole of diameter $d=1\ \mathrm{cm}$ has formed in the centre of the bottom of a rectangular barge of length $a=80\ \mathrm{m}$, width $b=10\ \mathrm{m}$ and height $c=5\ \mathrm{m}$. Estimate the time in which the barge will sink if the water is not pumped out. The barge is open at the top, there is no cargo on it, the initial height of the sides above the water level is $h=3.75\ \mathrm{m}$.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

Resistors $R, 2R, 3R, \dots, 100R$ are connected in series. The ends of this chain are connected together, after which one of the wires coming from a battery with emf $\mathcal{E}$ and zero internal resistance is connected to the point of their junction. Between which resistors $nR$ and $(n+1)R$ should the second wire coming from the battery be connected so that the current through the battery is the smallest?

Problem 1

During the first $t$ seconds the ball has travelled a path $s$. How many times did it manage to hit the plane during this time? The acceleration of free fall is $g$.

At some moment the string, which can be considered straight, makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal, and the kite is rising vertically upwards with speed $v$. What is, at this moment, the speed of a knot on the string which is at distances $L$ from the reel and $l$ from the kite?

problems.title: Problem 2

Problem 2

On one side of a cassette tape, from beginning to end without gaps, $N=45$ short songs are recorded, each with a duration of $t=1$ min. The time of fast winding of the tape from beginning to end with constant angular velocity of rotation of the driving spindle is $T_1=2$ min 45 s. Which song will we reach if we wind the tape forward from the very beginning for $T_2=1$ min 50 s? For this cassette the radius of the spindle with the whole tape wound on it is $R=25\ \mathrm{mm}$, and without the tape it is $r=10\ \mathrm{mm}$.

A force $F=10\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied to the free end of the thread. Find the acceleration of the stand if the portions of the thread not touching the pulley are horizontal, and the coefficient of friction between the body and the stand is $\mu=0.3$.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

The voltage of the electric mains in an apartment is $220\ \mathrm{V}$. A 9th-grade student decided to make a Christmas-tree garland. Among his supplies he found one lamp ($36\ \mathrm{V}/40\ \mathrm{W}$), 220 lamps ($3.5\ \mathrm{V}/0.28\ \mathrm{A}$) and many connecting wires whose resistance is negligible. What circuit, including the $36\ \mathrm{V}$ lamp and the minimum number of $3.5\ \mathrm{V}$ lamps, must he assemble so that all the lamps in his garland burn at normal incandescence? A lamp is considered to burn at normal incandescence if the voltage drop across it differs from the voltage for which it is rated by no more than 1%.

Neglect the internal resistance of the battery.

The vessel almost instantly acquires a speed $u$ and moves translationally. After thermal equilibrium has been established, the air in the vessel has humidity $r = 50\%$. Find the speed $u$. problems.title: Problem 5
problems.problem:
Problem 5

Acetone and benzene mix with each other in any proportions, forming a transparent solution. The volume of the mixture equals the total volume of the components before mixing. The refractive index $n$ of the mixture depends on the concentrations of acetone molecules $N_\mathrm{A}$ and benzene molecules $N_\mathrm{B}$ as follows:
$$n^2 = 1 + K_\mathrm{A} N_\mathrm{A} + K_\mathrm{B} N_\mathrm{B},$$
where $K_\mathrm{A}$ and $K_\mathrm{B}$ are some constants (the polarizabilities of the acetone and benzene molecules).

A flask contains $V = 200\ \mathrm{mL}$ of a mixture of acetone and benzene at temperature $T_1 = 50\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A glass rod immersed in the flask is illuminated with light of wavelength $\lambda = 546\ \mathrm{nm}$ and is not visible in this solution at this temperature. How many millilitres, and of which liquid, acetone or benzene, must be added to the flask after it has cooled to temperature $T_2 = 20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, so that after stirring the solution the glass rod is not visible under the same illumination? The refractive indices of light of this wavelength for these liquids at temperature $T_2$ are $n_\mathrm{A} = 1.36$ and $n_\mathrm{B} = 1.50$ respectively, and for glass $n_\mathrm{G} = 1.47$. The volume expansion coefficients of both liquids in the temperature range from $T_2$ to $T_1$ are the same and equal to $\mu = 0.00124\ \mathrm{1/K}$. Neglect the thermal expansion of the glass and the evaporation of the liquids.

Two closed vessels of capacities $V_1=10$ litres and $V_2=20$ litres have rigid walls and are kept at the same constant temperature $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The vessels are connected by a short tube with a tap. Initially the tap is closed. The first vessel contains air at a pressure $p_1=2\ \mathrm{atm}$ and relative humidity $r_1=20\%$. The second vessel contains air at a pressure $p_2=1\ \mathrm{atm}$ and relative humidity $r_2=40\%$. The tap is opened gradually, so that the process of equalisation of the pressures in the vessels can be considered isothermal. Find the minimum and the maximum relative humidity of the air in the vessel of capacity 10 litres.

Problem 3

A charged particle was moving in a region of space containing mutually perpendicular uniform fields: an electric field of strength $E$, a magnetic field of induction $B$, and the gravitational field $g$. The velocity vector of the particle was constant and perpendicular to the magnetic field. After the particle left this region and began to move in another region, where only the gravitational field $g$ is present, its speed began to decrease. How long after the particle leaves the first region will its speed reach its minimum value?

One of the plates of a plane capacitor, in the form of a square with side $a$, is fixed horizontally, and a large thin sheet of dielectric with dielectric constant $\varepsilon$ is placed on it. Charges $+Q$ and $-Q$ are placed on the plates of the capacitor, and the system is brought to equilibrium. The upper plate is displaced horizontally by a distance $x\ll a$ parallel to one of the sides of the square and released without initial velocity. Find the period of oscillation of this plate. The thickness $d$ of the dielectric is much smaller than the displacement $x$ of the upper plate. The plates have no electrical resistance.

The artificial lens is made so that it lets its owner see distant objects clearly without spectacles. Unlike the natural lens, whose surface curvature can change (the eye then focuses on the chosen objects; this is called accommodation), the artificial lens is rigid and cannot "readjust". Estimate the optical power of spectacles that would make it possible to read a book at a distance $d=0.3\ \mathrm{m}$ from the eye without difficulty.

A boy stands near one of the walls in an arch and throws a ball from point $A$, located at a height $h=170\ \mathrm{cm}$ above the ground. The initial speed of the ball is $v_0=15\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The ball returned to the point of throwing after $t=3\ \mathrm{s}$, having described the trajectory shown in the figure. What is the distance $D$ between the walls of the arch? All collisions are instantaneous and absolutely elastic, air resistance is to be neglected, the acceleration of free fall is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2010-5-1-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

A light thin-walled bowl in the shape of a rectangular parallelepiped with edge lengths $a$, $b$ and $c$ is freely suspended on a horizontal axis so that the bottom face of the bowl, with dimensions $a\times c$, is horizontal, and the top is open (that is, absent -- see the figure). The axis passes perpendicular to the faces of the parallelepiped with dimensions $a\times b$, in their plane of symmetry, at a distance $h<b/2$ from the bottom face $a\times c$. The bowl begins to be filled with water at the rate $v\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$. After what time will the bowl tip over, turning about the axis? What will happen to it afterwards if the rate of filling does not change?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2010-5-2-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

Two identical barrels contain the same amount of water. The temperature of the water in the first barrel is $t_1=20^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and in the second barrel $t_2=60^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Some amount of water was poured from the first barrel into the second, and the temperature $t=50^\circ\mathrm{C}$ was established in it. Then the same amount of water was poured from the second barrel into the first, so that there was again the same amount of water in the barrels. What temperature will be established in the first barrel? All heat losses to the surroundings and the mechanical work done in pouring are to be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

A modern laboratory power supply works as follows: first the values of the current $I_0$ and the voltage $U_0$ are set on it. After a load is connected, the unit itself chooses one of two modes: either it keeps the voltage across the load equal to $U_0$, if the current through the load is then not greater than $I_0$ -- or it keeps the current through the load equal to $I_0$, if the voltage across the load is then not greater than $U_0$. At what load resistance $R$ will the greatest power $W_{\max}$ be dissipated in it, and what is it equal to?

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

A uniform cone of mass $m$, with base radius $R$ and apex angle $2\alpha$, lies on its side on a horizontal table. To slowly stand the cone on its apex, in the position in which its axis is vertical, work $A$ must be done. What minimum work $A_1$ must be done to stand the cone from the initial position onto its base?

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

What horizontal force $F$ must be applied to the end of the thread at point $A$ of the system shown in the figure so that the load of mass $m_2$ does not come off its support, and the thread, to whose other end the load of mass $m_1$ is attached, remains taut? What can the acceleration $\vec a$ of the load $m_1$ be in this case? The thread is weightless and inextensible, the pulleys are weightless, there is no friction, the acceleration of free fall is $g$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2010-6-2-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

Water and water vapour at a temperature of $100^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are in a cylinder under a piston. Outside the cylinder there is a vacuum, and a weight of mass $m=100\ \mathrm{kg}$ stands on the piston, creating a pressure $p=10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ inside the cylinder. What quantity of heat $Q$ must be given to the mixture to raise the weight by a height $h=1\ \mathrm{m}$ from its initial position? The specific heat of vaporisation of water is $L=2.26\cdot10^6\ \mathrm{J/kg}$, the density of water vapour at $100^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $\rho=0.58\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

Vova and Dima decided to make a device for measuring the resistance of resistors -- an ``ohmmeter''. For this they took a battery with a known constant voltage $U=1.5\ \mathrm{V}$, a resistor with a known resistance $R=150\ \Omega$, a milliammeter with a range from 0 mA to 20 mA, connecting wires and two terminals for connecting the resistance to be measured. Draw what possible circuits Vova and Dima can assemble from these elements, and explain how, in these circuits, the milliammeter readings can be converted into the value of the resistance $R_x$ being measured.

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

A rigid wedge of mass $M$ lies on a smooth horizontal surface; its smooth inclined face makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal. A rigid ball of the same mass $M$ hits the wedge; an instant before it collides with the inclined face, the ball's velocity was horizontal. The collision is perfectly elastic. What angle $\beta$ with the horizontal will the ball's velocity make immediately after the collision?

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

A train approaching a station moves with uniform deceleration $a=0.2\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ right up to the moment it stops. On an absolutely smooth horizontal table inside a carriage of the train there is a small block connected by a spring to a fixed support (see figure). While the train is moving, the block is at rest relative to the carriage. At the moment the train stops, the block starts to move and oscillates with period $T=1\ \mathrm{s}$. Find the amplitude of the oscillations of the block.

The temperatures at points 1, 2 and 3 are, respectively, $T_1=300\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_2=500\ \mathrm{K}$, $T_3=800\ \mathrm{K}$. In the section 4-1 the gas gives up to the cooler the amount of heat $Q_{41}\approx 1172\ \mathrm{J}$. Find the efficiency of the cycle.

Problem 4

The section AB of an electric circuit consists of resistors with resistances $R_1=R_0$, $R_2=9R_0$, $R_3=9R_0$, $R_4=R_0$, where $R_0=1\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$, and an ideal diode CD (see figure). The ideal diode passes current without resistance in the direction from C to D and does not pass current at all in the opposite direction. The section AB is connected to a source of alternating sinusoidal voltage $U_{AB}(t)=U_m\sin\omega t$, whose amplitude is $U_m=300\ \mathrm{V}$. What thermal power will be dissipated in this section?

A bead threaded on a fixed rod that makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal (see figure) has mass $m$ and charge $q$. The bead can slide along the rod with coefficient of friction $\mu$ and starts to move from rest, where $\mu<\tan\alpha$. The system is in a uniform magnetic field of induction $B$ whose lines are horizontal (perpendicular to the plane of the figure and directed into the figure). What maximum speed and what maximum acceleration will the bead have during its motion? The rod does not conduct current. Consider two cases: $q>0$ and $q<0$.

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

The working substance of a heat engine is some amount of water. The cycle on which the engine works is shown in the figure in $p$–$T$ coordinates (the dashed line shows the dependence of the saturated vapour pressure of water on temperature). It consists of an isobaric (1–2–3), an isochoric (3–4) and an isothermal (4–1) section. Find the efficiency of this cycle, assuming water to be a practically incompressible liquid.

Reminders: $p_1=101.3\ \mathrm{kPa}$ is the normal atmospheric pressure, the specific heat of vaporization of water (at $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$) is $L\approx 2.26\cdot 10^6\ \mathrm{J/kg}$, the molar mass of water is $\mu=18\ \mathrm{g/mol}$, the specific heat capacity of water is $c\approx 4.19\cdot 10^3\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot K)}$, the universal gas constant is $R\approx 8.31\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$, the heat capacity of one mole of water vapour at constant pressure is $4R$.

A small ball has an electric charge $q$ and is attached to one end of the rod by a thin non-conducting uncharged thread of length $R$. What is the tension of the thread if the system is in equilibrium? Assume $Q/q>0$. Neglect gravity.

A non-conducting spring of stiffness $k$, placed horizontally, is attached to the ball on the left. The ball is in a uniform electric field $\vec E$ directed as shown in the figure. In the equilibrium state the thread with the ball hangs vertically. Find the period of small oscillations of the ball in the plane of the figure.

problems.title: Problem 5
problems.problem:
Problem 5

A microwave radar antenna is arranged as follows: $N=100$ emitters of electromagnetic waves of wavelength $\lambda=2d$ are placed along a straight line at equal distances $d=2.5\ \mathrm{cm}$ from each other (see figure). Each of them emits a spherical wave, and the magnitude of the field strength of the $n$-th emitter ($0\le n\le N$) varies according to the law $E(t)=A\sin\left(\omega t-kr_n+n\frac{\pi}{2}\cos\Omega t\right)$, where $r_n$ is the distance from the given emitter, $k=2\pi/\lambda$ is the wave number, and $\Omega\ll\omega$. Find how the angle between the beam emitted by the radar in the plane of the figure and the normal to the chain of emitters depends on time. Estimate the angular width of the beam and its angular velocity.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2011-2-5-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

A school dynamometer ended up in far-away space; its body has mass $M=20\ \mathrm{g}$ and its spring has mass $m=10\ \mathrm{g}$. The hook fixed to the body is pulled with a force $F_1=5\ \mathrm{N}$ directed along the axis of the spring, and the hook at the free end of the spring is pulled with a force $F_2=2\ \mathrm{N}$ directed opposite to the force $F_1$. What will the dynamometer "show", that is, opposite which division of the scale will the indicator needle stop?

A rigid wedge of mass $M$ lies on a smooth horizontal surface; its smooth inclined face makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal. A rigid ball of mass $m$ hits the wedge; an instant before it collides with the inclined face, the ball's velocity was horizontal. The collision is perfectly elastic. For what ratio $m/M$ will the ball move in the vertical direction after the collision?

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

The schoolboy Kolya poured cold okroshka (a cold soup) with temperature $t_{\mathrm{okr}}=10\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ into a plate. The mass of the okroshka in the plate is $m=300\ \mathrm{g}$, and its specific heat capacity equals the specific heat capacity of water, $c_{\mathrm{w}}=4200\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot ^\circ C)}$. Kolya added hot potatoes, which had temperature $t_{\mathrm{pot}}=80\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, to the okroshka. The total heat capacity of the added potatoes is $C=450\ \mathrm{J/^\circ C}$. After thermal equilibrium was established, the temperature of the potatoes and the okroshka turned out to be $t=22\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. In which direction was more heat transferred in the heat exchange with the surroundings: from the contents of the plate to the surroundings or vice versa, and by how much more?

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

Video recordings of various physical experiments are now easy to find on the internet, for example the following one:

A group of students lets some heavy gas from a cylinder into a large trough up to the brim, then places on the surface of this gas in the trough a model of a ship bent from aluminium foil, and this "ship" floats like a real "Flying Dutchman"! Then the students scoop gas out of the trough with a ladle, pour it into the "ship", and it sinks.

Find what minimum molar mass $M$ this heavy gas must have so that a "ship" in the form of a rectangular parallelepiped (open at the top), bent from household aluminium foil of thickness $h=25\ \mathrm{\mu m}$, can float in it. The dimensions of the "ship": length $a=50\ \mathrm{cm}$, width $b=20\ \mathrm{cm}$, height of the sides $c=10\ \mathrm{cm}$. Assume that the excess pieces formed when bending the parallelepiped from a sheet of foil have been removed. The density of aluminium is $\rho_{\mathrm{Al}}=2.7\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$, the density of air under the given conditions is $\rho_{\mathrm{a}}=1.3\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the average molar mass of air is $M_{\mathrm{a}}=29\ \mathrm{g/mol}$.

At what distance $x$ will the ball and that end of the rod near which the ball was initially located be in the equilibrium position? problems.title: Problem 5

Problem 5

In an $N$-pole network (a circuit with $N$ terminals) each terminal is connected to every other terminal by a resistor of resistance $R$ (a circuit of the "polygon" type). It is known that this circuit is equivalent to a circuit of the "star" type with $N$ terminals, in which $N$ resistors of value $r$ have a common contact at the centre and are connected by their other contacts to the corresponding terminals (each resistor is connected to one terminal). How are $R$ and $r$ related to each other?

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

Standing at the edge of a deep precipice, a tourist throws a stone vertically upward. In its subsequent motion downward the stone passes the point of throwing and falls into the precipice. It is known that in the time interval $t=1\ \mathrm{s}$, counted from the moment of the throw, the stone travelled a distance $S=2.9\ \mathrm{m}$. Determine the initial speed given to the stone at the throw. Take the acceleration of free fall to be $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Neglect air resistance.

On an inclined plane surface making an angle $\alpha=60^\circ$ with the horizontal there is a small flat puck of mass $m=0.5\ \mathrm{kg}$, attached by a light thread of length $L=1\ \mathrm{m}$ to a point on this surface. The puck was pushed along the surface so that the thread is taut and the velocity of the puck is perpendicular to the thread. At some moment the puck has a horizontally directed velocity $V=2\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The coefficient of friction of the puck on the plane is $\mu=0.6$. What is the magnitude of the acceleration $a$ of the puck at this moment? What is the tension $F$ of the thread at this moment? The acceleration of free fall is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

The density of water is $\rho_{\mathrm{w}}=1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the density of ice is $\rho_{\mathrm{i}}=900\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the density of steel is $\rho_{\mathrm{s}}=7800\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$. problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

A Tu-160 aircraft, in weather that was windless over the whole Earth, took off from an airfield in Saint Petersburg. Throughout the whole 27-hour flight the aircraft stayed at the same altitude and kept the same speed in magnitude, $1000\ \mathrm{km/h}$, having made several mid-air refuellings. First it flew south for 6 hours, then east for 10 hours, then north for 6 hours, and during the last 5 hours of the flight its velocity was directed west. How much more time will the aircraft need, with the same speed in magnitude, to reach its home airfield along the shortest path? Saint Petersburg lies at latitude $60^\circ$, and the radius of the Earth is approximately $6400\ \mathrm{km}$.

problems.title: Problem 2

Problem 2

After the construction of the Pyramid of Cheops was completed, all its edges, according to legend, had the same length $A\approx 230\ \mathrm{m}$. The base of the pyramid is a square with side $A$. According to tradition, during the "Great Flood" the water level coincided with the apex of the pyramid. With what force did the water press on the northern lateral face of the pyramid? The density of water is $\rho=1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the acceleration of free fall is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

Note: the volume $V$ of a pyramid is calculated by the formula $V=\frac{1}{3}SH$, where $S$ is the area of the base of the pyramid.

Problem 1: Playing with a hula hoop

A "hula hoop" is a hoop that girls spin around the waist, and sportswomen also do other "tricks" with it. For example, they spin it in a vertical plane and push it away from themselves horizontally, after which the rotating hoop, slipping on the floor, moves away from them for some distance and comes back.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2013-2-1-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

There is a hypothesis according to which the sizes of insects are limited by the fact that they take in air through tracheal tubes opening onto the surface of the body (that is, their air intake is proportional to the area of the body surface). The consumption of oxygen, in turn, is proportional to the mass of the body. Thus one can conclude that when an insect is enlarged in length, height and width by the same factor, it can come to the point where it begins to "suffocate" from a lack of oxygen.

It is known that in the Carboniferous geological period the wingspan of the dragonfly Meganeura reached $65\ \mathrm{cm}$. According to scientists' suppositions, this was possible because the oxygen concentration in the atmosphere was then $35\%$, and not $21\%$ as now (at the same air density). Assuming that this was the maximum possible size for Carboniferous times, estimate the maximum possible wingspan of a modern dragonfly. Modern dragonflies have approximately the same density and body proportions as the dragonfly of the Carboniferous period, and require per unit mass no less oxygen.

Note: the answer will somewhat exceed the actual sizes of modern dragonflies because of other factors limiting the size of a dragonfly (for example, competition with birds).

The tritium nuclei (denoted T, with atomic mass 3) contained in the superheavy water are radioactive. When one mole of tritium nuclei decays, an energy $E=1.79\ \mathrm{GJ}$ is released, and every second in each mole of tritium $N=1.07\cdot 10^{15}$ of its nuclei decay. The molar isobaric heat capacities of superheavy water and of its vapour are almost the same as those of ordinary water ($C_{\mathrm{w}}=75.6\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$ and $C_{\mathrm{v}}=33.2\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$, respectively). The boiling temperature at normal pressure and the molar heat of vaporization are also close to the corresponding values for ordinary water ($T_2=100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $L=40\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$). How much time $\tau_1$ will it take to bring the water to the boil? For what time $\tau_2$ will the water boil? To what temperature $T_3$ will the contents of the vessel heat up after a time $\tau_3=2.5$ hours from the start of the experiment? What will the volume $V$ of the vessel be at that moment? Assume that all the energy released in the decay of tritium is transferred to the water. The Avogadro constant is $N_A=6\cdot 10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, the universal gas constant is $R=8.3\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$.

Problem 2

One mole of an ideal gas takes part in the cyclic process $1\to2\to3\to1$ of a refrigerating machine. In state 1 the gas has temperature $T_1$ and volume $V_1$. It is known that all transitions of the gas from one state to another are polytropic. The polytropic exponent of process $2-3$ is greater by one than the polytropic exponent of process $1-2$ and less by one than the polytropic exponent of process $3-1$. In process $1-2$ the volume of the gas decreases by a factor of $k$. One of the processes of the cycle is isothermal.

1) Determine the volume of the gas in state 3.

2) Draw on a $pV$-diagram the cycle corresponding to the condition of the problem, indicating for each of the processes its polytropic exponent.

3) What can the temperature of the gas in state 3 be equal to?

Reference: A polytropic process is a process during which the heat capacity of the gas does not change: $C=\mathrm{const}$. The equation of such a process has the form $pV^n=\mathrm{const}$, or $p_1V_1^n=p_2V_2^n$. The quantity $n$ is called the polytropic exponent.

Problem 2

Almost 40 years have passed since the writer Grigory Oster wrote his stories about four friends – the Monkey, the Baby Elephant, the Boa Constrictor and the Parrot. During this time the Baby Elephant has grown up and turned into an ELEPHANT, the Boa Constrictor has become even longer, the Parrot has grown old and hunched, and the Monkey now serves as a stuffed animal in a zoological museum. At their latest meeting the friends remembered how they used to measure the length of the boa constrictor, and decided to recall the old days. The Boa Constrictor, lying on a horizontal floor, calculated the distance from the floor to its centre of mass, and it turned out to be equal to 10 cm. The centre of mass of the Elephant turned out to be at a height of 2 m above the floor. The centre of mass of the Boa Constrictor and the Elephant taken together was at a height of 1.7 m. When the Parrot sat on the head of the elephant at a height of 3.5 m above the floor, the centre of mass of all three turned out to be higher by another 0.5 mm. What is the mass of the Boa Constrictor in Parrots, if the height of the Parrot is much smaller than the thickness of the Boa Constrictor?

Problem 1

At one of the charging points for executor robots on a planet of the Shedar star system, robots are served one at a time at a rate of 60 robots per hour (r/h). On one of the days robots arrived at the point during 8 hours. During the first hour they arrived at a rate of 70 r/h. During the second hour the arrival rate increased uniformly, reaching 80 r/h by its end. Then during the third hour the arrival rate decreased uniformly and dropped back to 70 r/h by its end. In the fourth hour the arrival rate fell uniformly, reaching 20 r/h by the end of the hour, and then remained so during the fifth and sixth hours. In the seventh hour there was again a uniform rise of the arrival rate, to 100 r/h at the end of the hour, and in the eighth hour a uniform decrease of the arrival rate to 60 r/h was observed. The robots strictly keep to the order of the queue, and after charging they leave the point at once.

Problem 1

Two self-propelled barges move uniformly over a lake in mutually perpendicular directions. The speed of one barge is $V_1=3\ \mathrm{m/s}$, and of the other $V_2=4\ \mathrm{m/s}$. On each barge an anemometer is installed — a device for measuring the magnitude of the wind speed. For some time the readings of the anemometers on each of the ships are taken every minute. From the results of the measurements it was found that the wind speed values obtained on the first barge did not exceed the speed $V_1$ of the barge, and on the second did not exceed $V_2$. What maximum value could the wind speed relative to the lake reach during the measurements? What angle $\alpha$ did the velocity $\vec V_1$ of the first barge make with the direction of the wind at the moment when the wind speed relative to the lake was maximal?

Find the magnitudes and directions of the accelerations with which the board and the block will start to move in this case. The influence of other forces may be neglected.

A Stirling cycle consists of two isochoric and two isothermal processes. To increase the efficiency of this cycle a regenerator is used: a heat reservoir to which the working substance (an ideal gas) gives some amount of heat $Q^*$ during isochoric cooling, and from which it receives the same amount of heat $Q^*$ during isochoric heating. The effectiveness of the regenerator is characterised by the coefficient $k=Q^*/Q_V$, where $Q_V$ is the total amount of heat received by the working substance in the isochoric heating stage. The efficiency of the cycle depends on the regeneration coefficient $k$.

Let the efficiency of a certain Stirling cycle with regeneration vary, depending on the coefficient $k$, from the minimum possible value $1/6$ to the maximum possible value $1/3$.

After laughing his fill, Vasya noticed that at certain distances from the mirror his image in it either becomes strongly blurred or turns out to be indistinct, and he cannot make himself out. To investigate this phenomenon, Vasya began to approach the mirror, walking from far away along its optical axis and observing the images of his eyes. The diameter of the mirror is $2H=3\ \mathrm{m}$, the radius of curvature of the reflecting surface is $R=15\ \mathrm{m}$, the distance from the floor to Vasya's eyes is $h=H=1.5\ \mathrm{m}$. In the electric circuit whose diagram is shown in the figure, the resistances of the constant resistors are not known, and the resistance of the variable resistor can change over a wide range, from zero to values much greater than the resistances of the other resistors. The battery is ideal. Between the contacts $A$ and $B$ an ideal voltmeter is connected first, which not only measures the voltage (the open-circuit voltage) but also shows its polarity. problems.title: Problem 5: Electrocaloric generator
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Electrocaloric generator

In electrodynamics, when dielectrics are described, the electric displacement vector $\mathbf{D}$ is introduced. The vector $\mathbf{D}$ quantitatively characterizes the field of the free charges only (!), while the vector $\mathbf{E}$ characterizes the field of the free charges and of the polarization charges arising in dielectrics. Usually the vector $\mathbf{D}$ is proportional to the vector $\mathbf{E}$. However, there exist materials (ferroelectrics) in which $\mathbf{D}$ depends on $\mathbf{E}$ nonlinearly. In this problem the vectors $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{E}$ are codirectional. The schematic form of the dependence $D(E)$ for a typical ferroelectric at constant temperature is shown in Fig. 5 by the black line. The dependence $D(E)$ for the same ferroelectric at a higher temperature is shown schematically by the grey line. Both dependences have a pronounced hysteresis, in other words, the value of $D$ for a given $E$ depends on the manner in which the field $E$ changes (increases or decreases). However, in this problem this is not essential.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2019-2-5-fig1.png

[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 5» = Fig. 5]

In some ferroelectrics the form of the dependence $D(E)$ changes very strongly with temperature, which makes it possible to use them for converting thermal energy into electrical energy. Let us connect a capacitor with a ferroelectric to an ideal source of constant voltage. By periodically changing the temperature of the ferroelectric, one can obtain a periodically varying current in the circuit. The work of the voltage source over a cycle will then be zero. One obtains a converter of thermal energy into the work of the current. One may regard the ferroelectric as a peculiar working body of a heat engine, characterized by the parameters $D$, $E$, $T$.

Consider the model cycle shown in Fig. 6. Processes 1–2 and 3–4 are the charging and discharging of the capacitor with the ferroelectric at constant temperature. 2–3 and 4–1 are heating and cooling at constant electric field. The cycle has the shape of a parallelogram.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2019-2-5-fig2.png

[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 6» = Fig. 6]

The thermodynamics of the ferroelectric is described by the relations valid for small (!) changes of the parameters $\Delta E$, $\Delta D$, $\Delta T$:
$$\Delta D=\varepsilon_0\varepsilon\,\Delta E+p\,\Delta T,\qquad \frac{\Delta Q}{V}=c\,\Delta T+pT\,\Delta E,\qquad \frac{\Delta A}{V}=D\,\Delta E,$$
where $\varepsilon$, $p$ and $c$ ($\varepsilon>0$, $p<0$, $c>0$) are known constant coefficients. The volume $V$ is considered constant. $\Delta Q$ and $\Delta A$ are the amount of heat and the work for small changes of the parameters. These relations are sufficient for solving the problem.

1) Determine the efficiency of the cycle 1234. Regard the quantities $E_\mathrm{L}$, $E_\mathrm{H}$ and $T_\mathrm{L}$, $T_\mathrm{H}$ as known ($T_\mathrm{L}<T_\mathrm{H}$). If one assumes that $E_\mathrm{L}$ and $E_\mathrm{H}$ can vary without limit, what is the maximum efficiency of this cycle? (7 points)

2) Draw qualitatively on the $D$–$E$ diagram the thermodynamic cycle $12'34'$, in which on the sections $1$–$2'$ and $3$–$4'$ the charging and discharging of the capacitor with the ferroelectric take place adiabatically. The temperatures at the points 1 and 3 are $T_\mathrm{L}$ and $T_\mathrm{H}$. (5 points)

3) Determine the efficiency of the cycle from part 2), regarding $E_\mathrm{L}$, $E_\mathrm{H}$ and $T_\mathrm{L}$, $T_\mathrm{H}$ as known, and the changes of the parameters $D$, $E$ and $T$ within the cycle as small. Which cycle has the greater efficiency for the same $E_\mathrm{L}$, $E_\mathrm{H}$, $T_1=T_\mathrm{L}$ and $T_3=T_\mathrm{H}$: $1234$ or $12'34'$? (6 points)

Problem 2: At the moment of a fall

In rock climbing, one end of the rope is tied to the safety harness worn by the climber who goes first (the leader); the rest of the rope is with the belayer. During the ascent the leader "clips" the rope trailing behind him through carabiners (metal rings with a gate) attached to the wall at protection points (point $B$ in Fig. 1). If the leader falls, the belayer, located at point $A$ (not shown in the figure), locks the rope with a belay device. The fall factor $r$ is the ratio of the depth of the leader's free fall (until the rope begins to stretch) to the length of the rope between the belayer and the leader at the moment of the fall; for example, $r=\dfrac{2h}{H+h}$ for the scheme in Fig. 1. Suppose that there is one protection point between the leader and the belayer (as in Fig. 1), or none at all ($H=0$). The positions of the leader and of the protection point may be arbitrary, but the quantity $h+H$ must be less than the length of the rope ($\approx 50\ \mathrm{m}$). The climbers are high above the ground, so the leader may fall below the belayer. Neglect friction between the rope and the carabiner.

[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 1» = Fig. 1]

3) In reality, at large elongations the rope does not obey Hooke's law. In a model fall of a load of mass $m$ in a laboratory with fall factor $r_1=1.5$, the maximum relative elongation was $40\,\%$. Let $W_{\mathrm{exp}}$ be the maximum deformation energy of the rope calculated on the basis of the test, and $W_{\mathrm{theor}}$ the deformation energy calculated on the basis of Hooke's law at the same relative elongation. Problem 4: Stirling engine

The problem considers a thermodynamic model of a Stirling engine, shown schematically in Fig. 4. Within the model its temperature is assumed to be maintained constant (denote it by $T$). A radiator 7 is attached to the displacer cylinder 2 to improve heat exchange; the temperature in this cylinder is taken to be equal to the room temperature $T_0$. The working substance 4 (air) is pumped from the working cylinder to the displacer cylinder and back through the tube 5. The device 6 is a special heat exchanger. When air flows from the working cylinder to the displacer cylinder, this heat exchanger accumulates the amount of heat that was not spent by the working substance on doing work in the working cylinder. Then this heat is returned completely to the air when it flows back from the displacer cylinder to the working cylinder. Therefore one may assume that the whole amount of heat received by the working substance from the heater is spent on doing work in the working cylinder. The maximum volume of air in the working cylinder is denoted $V_{01}$, and in the displacer cylinder $V_{02}$. The volume of the tube may be neglected.

Problem 1: From the history of power lines

In 1882, at the electrotechnical exhibition in Munich, the operation of the world's first long (several tens of kilometres) power transmission line was demonstrated. problems.title: Problem 1: Calculating the speed of light
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Calculating the speed of light

The first estimate of the speed of light was given by Rømer in 1675. Studying the motion of Io (a satellite of Jupiter), he obtained a value close to $220000\ \mathrm{km/s}$. The orbit of Io lies in the plane of the Earth's orbit, therefore the satellite periodically disappears in the shadow of Jupiter. The interval between two successive emergences of Io from the shadow of Jupiter is on average $42.5\ \mathrm{h}$. However, according to modern studies, for various positions of the Sun, the Earth and Jupiter this interval can deviate from the average value by no more than $16\ \mathrm{s}$ in either direction. From the data presented, determine the speed of light if the distance from the Earth to the Sun is $1.5\cdot10^{8}\ \mathrm{km}$. Problem 2: The Kelvin–Varley divider

Fig. 1 shows the diagram of a Kelvin–Varley voltage divider. The resistances of the resistors of one column (the columns are shown by dashed lines) are identical, and in different columns they are different. If a constant voltage $U_0$ is applied to the terminals $A$ and $B$, then the voltage at the terminals $C$ and $D$ will be $U_1=\alpha U_0$, where the value of the coefficient $\alpha$ ($0<\alpha<1$) depends on the position of the contacts marked by black arrows. By changing the positions of the contacts, the value of the coefficient $\alpha$ can be set to an accuracy of one ten-thousandth. Between neighbouring contacts (in all columns except the last) there must always be one free terminal. For the position of the contacts shown in the figure by black arrows, $\alpha=0.2073$. If the position of the contacts in the second column is changed as shown by the light-grey arrows, the multiplication coefficient becomes $\alpha=0.2573$. The position of the contacts in the first column determines the digit in the tenths place of the value of the coefficient $\alpha$, in the second column the digit in the hundredths place, and so on. Assuming the resistance $R$ of the resistors in the last column to be known, determine the resistances of the resistors in the other columns. For what position of the contacts will the coefficient $\alpha$ be equal to $\alpha_0=0.2019$?

problems.title: Problem 3: Vapour film and nucleate boiling
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Vapour film and nucleate boiling

A steel ball ($m=110\ \mathrm{g}$, $R=1.5\ \mathrm{cm}$, $c=500\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot{}^\circ C)}$), heated to a temperature $T_1=500^\circ\mathrm{C}$, lies on a heat-insulating stand in a transparent vessel, which is filled with distilled water ($m_0=0.4\ \mathrm{kg}$, $T_0=20^\circ\mathrm{C}$) so that the ball is approximately in the middle of the water column. An interesting phenomenon is observed. A thin vapour film forms around the ball very quickly; after this, for some time the thickness of the film remains constant, equal to $d=0.5\ \mathrm{mm}$, the formation of vapour bubbles (as in boiling) is not observed, and heat exchange between the water and the ball takes place through the film. At the moment when the temperature of the ball decreases to $T_2=250^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the film "breaks down" and vigorous boiling begins in the liquid near the ball, which continues until the temperature of the ball decreases to $T_\mathrm{b}=100^\circ\mathrm{C}$. One may assume that in the processes of film formation and nucleate boiling all the heat given up by the ball goes into the evaporation of water, but one third of the vapour in the rising bubbles (formed during boiling) condenses. Heat exchange with the surroundings and the heat-insulating stand, as well as heating of the vapour, may be neglected. Determine the temperature of the water at the moment when heat exchange between the ball and the water ends. The specific heat capacity and the heat of vaporization of water are $c_0=4200\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot{}^\circ C)}$ and $L=2.2\cdot10^{6}\ \mathrm{J/kg}$. The average density of the vapour is $\rho\approx0.6\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$. The volume of a ball of radius $R$ is determined by the formula $V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-1-4-fig2.png

2) Assuming that the ratio $\alpha=\dfrac{R_l}{r+R_0}$ is known ($\alpha>1$), determine the maximum value of the current through the motor in this case. (4 points)

3) When the motor is switched off (after the rotation speed of the shaft has settled), first the switch $K_1$ is opened. At this moment the voltage across the terminals of the motor increases almost instantly by $\Delta U_{AB}=2\ \mathrm{V}$. Determine the parameter $\alpha$ from these data. (3 points)

The circuit shown in the third figure is the closest to a real device. The switches are initially open. Turning the ignition key corresponds to closing the switch $K_1$. When the current through the coil $L$ reaches some threshold value $I_{\mathrm{th}}$, the switch $K_2$ closes (the magnetic field of the coil draws in a rod that closes the contacts of the switch $K_2$).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-1-4-fig3.png

4) The inductance of the second coil $L$ and its resistance $R_L$ are such that $L=10l$, $R_l=5R_L$. It is known that the value of the current $I_{\mathrm{th}}$ lies between 10 A and 20 A. What is the current through the coil of inductance $l$ at the moment of closing of the switch $K_2$? Take the numerical value of the parameter $\alpha$ as known from part 3). (2 points)

problems.title: Problem 5: Vacuum gun
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Vacuum gun

In recent years the device called the “vacuum gun” has attracted great interest among enthusiasts of scientific and technical creativity. In a polypropylene water pipe 2 (see the figure below), one end of which is hermetically closed by a foil plug 3 and the other is open to the atmosphere, a ping-pong ball 1 is accelerated by the pressure difference. The inner diameter of the pipe is close to the diameter of the ball. Next to the plug there is a fitting 4 through which the pipe is connected to a vacuum pump. Thus the pressure to the right of the ball is very low, while at the open end of the pipe the pressure is close to atmospheric, equal to $P_0$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-1-5-fig1.png

It turns out that with a sufficiently long pipe and good evacuation the ball can be accelerated to a high speed, so that it easily tears the foil plug and flies out of the pipe. One video available online demonstrates how the ball flying out of the pipe pierces empty soda cans placed at a small distance from the pipe.

1) In the crudest model it is assumed that to the left of the ball the pressure is equal to $P_0=10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, and to the right it is equal to zero. The pressure difference does not change during the acceleration of the ball. There is no friction between the ball and the walls of the pipe. To what maximum speed $v_{\max}^{(1)}$ can a ball of mass $M=2.7\ \mathrm{g}$ and diameter $d=40\ \mathrm{mm}$ be accelerated in a pipe of length $L=2\ \mathrm{m}$? (1 point)

In a more accurate model it is assumed that under the action of the constant pressure difference not only the ball is accelerated, but also the air of mass $m(t)$ located at time $t$ in the pipe to the left of the ball, and in addition new portions of air from the atmosphere are drawn into the motion. It is proposed to assume that the region near the left end of the pipe in which the air is drawn into the motion has a small characteristic size, comparable to the diameter of the pipe. Outside the pipe, beyond this region, the air remains at rest. Inside the pipe the air moves with the speed of the ball, and its density is equal to the density $\rho$ of the air outside. The diameter of the ball is much smaller than the length of the pipe. At the initial moment the coordinate $x$ of the ball and its speed are equal to zero.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-1-5-fig2.png

2) Determine a more accurate value of the speed $v_{\max}^{(2)}$ to which a ball of the same dimensions as in part 1) of the problem can be accelerated in a pipe of the same length. The acceleration time can be taken in the first approximation to be equal to the acceleration time in part 1). The temperature of the air and its molar mass are $T_0=293\ \mathrm{K}$, $\mu=29\ \mathrm{g/mol}$, respectively. (3 points)

3) Assuming that only the temperature $T_0=293\ \mathrm{K}$ outside the pipe and the molar mass of air $\mu=29\ \mathrm{g/mol}$ are known, determine the maximum speed to which the ball can be accelerated. The pipe is assumed to be sufficiently long. (3 points)

4) The parameters are given: $M$, $S$, $P_0$, $\rho$, $\mu$. Obtain the formula for the dependence of the coordinate of the ball on time $x(t)$. (5 points)

Note. The formula $\Delta(x^2)=2x\Delta x$, valid for small changes ($\Delta x\ll x$) of the quantity $x$, may turn out to be useful.

Interestingly, a group from Purdue University (USA), having slightly complicated the design, managed to accelerate the ball to a supersonic speed ($v\approx420\ \mathrm{m/s}$, which is $\mathrm{M}=1.23$ times the speed of sound), so that after flying out of the pipe the table-tennis ball pierced a table-tennis racket. The video can be found online by the phrase: «Purdue Technology students build supersonic ping pong gun». In the improved design there is a cylinder of compressed air at the left end of the pipe and a Laval nozzle through which the air enters the “barrel of the gun”.

problems.title: Problem 1: Oscillations inside a pipe
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Oscillations inside a pipe

Inside a horizontally placed pipe of radius $R$, rotating with some angular velocity about its axis of symmetry, there is a small body. In the equilibrium position the body is located below the axis of the pipe, at a distance $0.8R$ from it vertically. Find the period of small oscillations of the body in the plane perpendicular to the axis of the pipe.

Note. For a small angle $\delta$ ($\delta\ll1$) and an arbitrary angle $\alpha$ the following approximate equalities hold: $\sin(\alpha+\delta)\approx\sin\alpha+\delta\cos\alpha$, $\cos(\alpha+\delta)\approx\cos\alpha-\delta\sin\alpha$.

problems.title: Problem 2: A table on thin legs
problems.problem:
Problem 2: A table on thin legs

A table stands on a horizontal floor. The tabletop and the floor can be considered absolutely rigid, and the legs elastic, obeying Hooke's law for vertical deformations.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-2-fig1.png

A weight of mass 24 kg is placed on the table so that its centre of mass is located at point $A$ (see the figure, top view). By how much do the forces of pressure of the table legs on the floor, $\Delta F_1$, $\Delta F_2$, $\Delta F_3$ and $\Delta F_4$, change after this? The numbers of the legs are shown in the figure.

problems.title: Problem 3: Water-steam-water
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Water-steam-water

Water of mass $m=180\ \mathrm{g}$ at constant pressure $p_1=10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ is given some amount of heat, so that it turns into steam and is heated to the temperature $T_1=105\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Then the steam expands adiabatically and at some moment reaches the saturation state, after which it condenses. The graph of the saturated vapour pressure of water against temperature is shown in the figure below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-3-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Па» = Pa; the axes are pressure $P$ in $10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and temperature $T$ in °C]

Assuming that the change of the parameters of the steam during the adiabatic expansion is small, determine approximately the temperature of the water at the beginning of condensation.

What is the total work of the steam during its heating after evaporation and cooling until the beginning of condensation? The molar heat capacity of the steam at constant volume is $c_V=3R$.

Note. Take into account that for small changes $\Delta p$ and $\Delta V$ of the quantities $p$ and $V$ the approximate formula $\Delta(pV)=p\Delta V+V\Delta p$ holds.

problems.title: Problem 4: Caustics
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Caustics

A caustic is the envelope of a family of rays that do not intersect at one point. In the planar case considered in this problem, a caustic is a curve to which all the rays reflected from some surface, or refracted at some interface, are tangent. The intensity of light near caustics increases, so caustic curves are clearly visible to the naked eye and in photographs.

1. The grey curve in the figure is the caustic formed after the reflection of a beam of parallel rays by the cylindrical surface $M$ of radius $R$. Determine the distance from the axis of the cylinder, point $O$, to the vertex of the caustic, point $A$, and also the distance $PA$. $OO_1$ is the axis of symmetry, $P_1P_2$ is a tangent to the caustic. (5 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-4-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «К п. 1» = For part 1]

2. A source illuminating a cylindrical surface of radius $R$ is located at a distance $a=4R$ from point $O$ on the axis of symmetry $OO_1$ of the system. Determine the distance from point $O$ to the vertex of the caustic formed by the reflected rays in this case. (4 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-4-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «К п. 2» = For part 2]

Water is poured into a thin-walled glass cylindrical beaker and illuminated with the light of a lamp. The axis of the light beam makes different angles $\alpha$ with the horizontal surface of the table in part 3 and part 4. In part 3 the beaker is photographed from above (the optical axis of the lens is perpendicular to the bottom of the beaker) and is illuminated from the right. In part 4 the axis of the lens is slightly tilted from the perpendicular.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-4-fig3.png
[Labels in the figure: «К п. 3» = For part 3]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-4-fig4.png
[Labels in the figure: «К п. 4» = For part 4]

3. The angle $\alpha$ is about $45^\circ$. Near the bottom of the beaker a curve with two vertices is observed, parts of which resemble the curve from part 1. In the figure the vertices are marked with squares. Explain the observed picture. (3 points)

4. The radius of the base of the beaker is $R=8\ \mathrm{cm}$. The lamp is located at a distance $a\approx10R$ from the axis of the beaker. The angle $\alpha$ can be considered small. Outside the beaker a caustic formed by the rays that have passed through the beaker is visible. Determine approximately the distance from the beaker to the vertex of the caustic (to the vertex of the “cone”). The refractive index of water is $n\approx1.33$. (6 points)

problems.title: Problem 5: Thermal inductor
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Thermal inductor

A Peltier element consists of two plates separated by a large number of semiconductor blocks (figure from Wikipedia below) and is a converter of electrical energy into thermal energy. It can also work in the reverse mode, generating an emf when there is a temperature difference between the plates.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-5-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «горячая пластина» = hot plate; «холодная пластина» = cold plate]

The second figure shows schematically a device based on a Peltier element. The lower plate is in contact with a “heat reservoir”, a large body whose temperature $T_r$ can be considered constant. The upper plate is in contact with a body of heat capacity $C$ and temperature $T$, which varies with time. A superconducting coil of inductance $L$ is connected between the contacts of the element. At the initial moment $T=T_0$, $T_0>T_r$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-2-5-fig2.png

Under these conditions the upper body gives the element, during the time $\Delta t$, the amount of heat $\Delta Q=\alpha TI\Delta t$, where $\alpha$ is a constant coefficient and $I$ is the current through the element. The positive direction of the current is the direction from “plus” to “minus”. The Peltier element in this case generates an emf equal to $\mathcal{E}=\alpha(T-T_r)$. The polarity of the generated emf (for $T>T_r$) coincides with that indicated in the figure. The resistance of the Peltier element is $R$.

It turns out that in the system considered a periodic variation of the temperature of the body $T(t)$ and of the current in the circuit $I(t)$ is possible. In this problem it is proposed to study the oscillations of the current and of the temperature for various values of the parameters $T_r$, $T_0$, $C$, $\alpha$, $R$, which are considered known. The current in the circuit at the initial moment is equal to zero: $I(0)=0$. The difference between the temperatures of the body and of the reservoir can be considered small: $|T-T_r|\ll T_r$ at any moment.

1. Consider an idealized, fantastic case, when the resistance $R$ is equal to zero and there is no heat exchange between the heat reservoir and the body by heat conduction.

1a) Obtain a differential equation for the function $I(t)$. (2 points)

1b) Transform the equation obtained taking into account the condition $|T-T_r|\ll T_r$ and find the frequency $\omega_0$ of the oscillations of the current. (3 points)

1c) Find the dependence of the temperature of the body on time $T(t)$. (1 point)

2. Physically, the case described in part 1 is never realized. Consider parameters of the system close to reality. Let the resistance of the element $R$ be known, the power of heat transfer from the body to the reservoir be given by the relation $P=k(T-T_r)$, where $k$ is a known coefficient, and the Joule heat released in the element be divided equally between the plates. In this case the oscillations will be damped.

2a) Obtain a differential equation for the function $I(t)$ in this case. (3 points)

2b) Show that the nonlinear terms proportional to $I^2$ and $I\dot{I}$ (the dot denotes the time derivative) in the equation from part 2a) can be neglected, and transform the equation obtained to the form $\ddot{I}+2\gamma\dot{I}+\omega^2I=0$ (the equation of damped oscillations). What are the coefficients $\gamma$ and $\omega$? (4 points)

2c) Assuming the damping to be weak ($\gamma^2\ll\omega^2$), determine the relative change of the amplitude of the current over a period, $\dfrac{\Delta I_{\max}}{I_{\max}}$. Express the answer through the coefficients $\gamma$ and $\omega$. (3 points)

3. It is proposed to create on the basis of this device an installation for accurate measurement of the heat capacity of bodies. The parameters $T_r$, $\alpha$, $k$, $R$, $L$ are known. They were measured earlier with high accuracy. The experimenter has electrical measuring instruments, an oscilloscope and an alternating voltage generator whose frequency can be varied over a wide range. Describe in a few words a possible scheme of the experiment. (2 points)

problems.title: Problem 1: Measuring deviations
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Measuring deviations

The resistance of a thermistor depends strongly on temperature (the graph is shown in the figure), therefore thermistors are used in precise meters of the deviation of temperature $\Delta T$ from a given value $T_0$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-4-1-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «R, кОм» = $R$, $\mathrm{k\Omega}$; «T,°C» = $T$, °C]

The circuit of the meter is shown in the second figure. The thermistor is denoted $R_t$. The resistance of the variable resistor $R_1$ can be varied in the range from 0 to 900 $\Omega$. The terminals are connected to an ideal source with voltage $U_0=6\ \mathrm{V}$. Before the measurement of the deviation $\Delta T$ from the temperature $T_0$ the meter is calibrated by choosing the resistance of the resistor $R_1$ so that the ideal pointer millivoltmeter shows zero. Later, when the temperature changes by $\Delta T$, the resistance of the thermistor changes and the millivoltmeter shows the voltage $U$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-4-1-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «0 В» = 0 V]

1) For the temperature $T_0=50\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ determine the dependence $U(\Delta T)$, assuming the change of the resistance of the thermistor to be small. In the region of which temperatures (high or low) does the meter provide a smaller relative error of measurement? (7 points)

Note. The approximate formula $(1+x)^{-1}\approx1-x$, valid for small $x$ ($x\ll1$), may turn out to be useful.

2) In what temperature range can this meter operate if it is undesirable for the thermal power released in the thermistor to exceed $P_0=0.15\ \mathrm{W}$? (3 points)

problems.title: Problem 2: A boy with a balloon
problems.problem:
Problem 2: A boy with a balloon

The boy Vlad runs in a circle, holding in his hand the end of a thread of length $2\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{m}$, to the other end of which a small inflated balloon with helium inside is attached. Vlad runs one circle in $2\pi$ seconds. The hand holding the thread moves along a circle of radius 2 m. The balloon moves along a circle of the same radius, 2 metres above the hand vertically. With what steady speed will the balloon rise if the thread is released?

One may assume that the air resistance force is proportional to the square of the speed, and the radius of the balloon is much smaller than the length of the thread. The acceleration of free fall is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

problems.title: Problem 3: Aeolipile
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Aeolipile

The aeolipile (a steam engine invented in Ancient Greece) is a metal boiler with two tubes on the lid, on which, as on an axis, a turbine in the form of a hollow sphere with two identical L-shaped pipes (nozzles) can rotate. Water is poured into the boiler, it is hermetically closed and put on a fire. The water vapour formed on boiling enters the sphere through the tubes and comes out with high speed through the nozzles, making the sphere rotate (see the figure from Wikipedia). Let the power of heat supply to the water be $P=1\ \mathrm{kW}$, the cross-sectional area of a pipe $S=0.1\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, and the distance from the nozzle to the axis of rotation $d=10\ \mathrm{cm}$. Assume that saturated steam at atmospheric pressure $p_0=10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ comes out of the nozzle. Friction in the axis and air resistance can be neglected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-4-3-fig1.png

1) Determine the torque exerted on the sphere by the steam if the sphere is fixed.

2) What maximum number of revolutions per minute will the sphere make if it is allowed to rotate freely?

problems.title: Problem 4: Car mirror
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Car mirror

When light is incident on the air-glass interface (the refractive index of the glass is $n=1.5$) at a small angle to the normal, a fraction equal to $R=4\,\%$ of the energy of the incident radiation is reflected, and $T=96\,\%$ of the energy passes into the second medium. It does not matter in which direction the light propagates: from air to glass or from glass to air.

A glass wedge (prism) of size $d=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ with a small apex angle $\varphi=0.06$ rad is leaned against an ideal mirror (one that reflects all the incident light) (see the figure). A laser beam directed along the normal to the mirror is incident on the prism. On a screen of height $H=40\ \mathrm{cm}$, placed parallel to the mirror at a distance $L=1\ \mathrm{m}$ from it, several spots of different brightness are observed. The refractive index of the glass is $n=1.5$. The vertical distance from the laser beam to the lower edge of the screen is $h=25\ \mathrm{cm}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-4-4-fig1.png

1) Find approximately the distance from the upper edge of the screen to each spot and calculate the fraction of the energy of the incident radiation (in percent, rounded to integers) carried by the rays forming this spot. Take into account that the approximate relations $\sin\alpha\approx\alpha$ and $\tan\alpha\approx\alpha$ hold with good accuracy even for angles of about 0.4 rad. (6 points)

2) Through what angle should the mirror with the prism be rotated in the plane of the figure so that in place of the brightest spot there appears another one, the next in brightness? (3 points)

3) In 1958 the Chrysler company used a mirror with a prism as a rear-view mirror with two modes of operation. With the help of a special lever it could be switched from the “day” mode to the “night” mode, so that the light of the headlights of cars driving behind, reflected by the mirror, did not dazzle the driver. Explain the principle of operation of such a car mirror. (1 point)

problems.title: Problem 5: Freezer with a hot wall
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Freezer with a hot wall

The rear wall of a not very modern freezer, on which the tubes of the condenser of the refrigerating machine operating on a reversed Carnot cycle are located, gets warm, so that its mean temperature $T_S$ in the working mode is higher than the temperature $T_R$ in the room. Inside the freezing chamber the refrigerating machine maintains the mean temperature $T_C=-23\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

It is known that in the steady state, when the temperature of the rear wall and the temperature in the chamber have settled, and the temperature in the room does not change with time, the compressor motor of this not very modern freezer works without stopping.

In hot weather, when the temperature in the room rises to $T_R^{(0)}=+27\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the rear wall heats up to $T_S^{(0)}=+47\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Determine the temperature of the rear wall of the freezer in winter on a cold day, when the air temperature in the room decreases to the value $T_R^{(1)}=+17\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

The power of heat transfer from a hot body to a cold one (for example, from the room air to the freezing chamber through the thermal insulation) is proportional to the difference of the corresponding temperatures.

problems.title: Problem 1: The chair starts to tip over
problems.problem:
Problem 1: The chair starts to tip over

A thin strip (about 1 cm high) is nailed to a smooth horizontal floor. Vasya put a chair against the strip with its front legs, tied a rope to the top point of the back of the chair, and with the help of a dynamometer found out that the chair starts to tip over when a horizontal force $F_1=16\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied to the rope perpendicular to the strip. Then he changed the position of the chair, and now the chair touches the strip with its rear legs. In this case the minimum value of the force, applied perpendicular to the strip in the horizontal direction, needed to tip the chair over turned out to be $F_2=12\ \mathrm{N}$. The distance between the legs of the chair (see the figure) is $a=42\ \mathrm{cm}$. The height of the top point of the back above the floor is $H=72\ \mathrm{cm}$. One may assume that this point is exactly above the line of the rear legs. What minimum force $F_3$ must be applied to the rope to tip the chair over if the chair is put against the strip with its right legs? Assume that the acceleration of free fall is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. The right and left halves of the chair are symmetric.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-6-1-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 2: The resistor starts to melt
problems.problem:
Problem 2: The resistor starts to melt

When the current through a wire resistor is increased, it heats up, and its temperature depends on the flowing current nonlinearly. At small currents, which for typical resistors are of the order of 10 mA, the temperature $T$ of the resistor is practically indistinguishable from the temperature $T_0$ of the environment. When the current is increased to some limiting value $I_{\max}$, the resistor very quickly (almost instantly) heats up to a very high temperature and melts (burns out).

Let the resistance of some resistor at room temperature and a current of 1 mA be equal to 10 $\Omega$. It is known that the value of the limiting current for this resistor is $I_{\max}=1.35\ \mathrm{A}$. Find the resistance of the resistor and the voltage across it at a current equal to $0.8I_{\max}$.

One may assume that the dependence of the resistance of the resistor on temperature is linear: $R(T)=R_0(1+\alpha(T-T_0))$, where $R_0$ is the resistance of the resistor at temperature $T_0$ and $\alpha$ is an unknown coefficient. The power of heat transfer is proportional to the difference between the temperatures of the resistor and of the environment.

problems.title: Problem 3: Rugby
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Rugby

Rugby is a team game with a ball. The aim of the game is to carry the ball into the opponent's in-goal area, located behind the goal line. A player with the ball may pass it to another player of his team, and the pass may not be made forward (only sideways or backward). Players of the opposing team have the right to stop the player with the ball. The figure shows a fragment of the field with three rugby players: $A$ and $B$ are players of one team, $C$ is a player of the opposing team. Player $C$ is about to stop player $A$, so the latter passes the ball to player $B$. To make an accurate pass, player $A$ has slowed down beforehand, and at the moment of the throw his velocity is directed towards the goal line and equals $v=2\ \mathrm{m/s}$.

Let the speed of player $B$ be 8 m/s when moving along any trajectory. The arrangement of players $A$, $B$ and $C$ on the field, shown in the figure, corresponds to the moment of the throw.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-6-3-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Зачетное поле соперника» = Opponent's in-goal area; «Линия ворот» = Goal line; «м» = m]

1) With what minimum speed (relative to himself) must player $A$ throw the ball so that player $B$ receives the pass and reaches the opponent's in-goal area in the minimum time? (2 points)

2) Let player $A$ throw the ball with a relative speed of 6 m/s. Prove that the minimum time $t_{\min}$ in which player $B$ can run to the in-goal area, catching the ball in the course of the motion, is achieved if after the throw by player $A$ the ball flies parallel to the goal line. (4 points)

3) Find the time $t_{\min}$. The statement of part 2) may be used without proof. (4 points)

problems.title: Problem 4: Vova starts calculating
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Vova starts calculating

Vova and his dad drove by car from Moscow to Saint Petersburg. On the highway the speed of their car was no more than 110 km/h but not less than 80 km/h. Out of boredom Vova decided to shoot a video on his smartphone. A jeep got into the frame, moving for some time in the adjacent lane with the same speed as the car of Vova's dad. And then Vova noticed that on the screen of his phone the radial crossbars on the disc of the wheel of the jeep (the shape of the disc is shown in the figure below) either stand still or rotate slowly, making no more than one revolution in about 10 s. Later, in the parking lot, from the marking on the tyre of the jeep that had overtaken them, Vova determined the diameter of its wheel, which turned out to be 72 cm. Vova knows that his smartphone shoots video at a rate of 30 frames per second. He assumes that each frame is an instantaneous photograph.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-6-4-fig1.png

Vova thought that from the available data he can not merely determine the speed $v$ of the jeep at the moment when it drew level with dad's car, but also indicate the limits of the interval $v_{\min}<v<v_{\max}$ within which the value of the speed $v$ lies.

1) What can the speed $v$ be equal to? One value is sufficient. (8 points)

2) Determine the limits of the interval $v_{\min}$ and $v_{\max}$ of the possible speeds. (2 points)

problems.title: Problem 5: The shadow starts to be attracted
problems.problem:
Problem 5: The shadow starts to be attracted

The experiment usually called “attracting shadows” is widely known. An extended light source illuminates two objects, and the shadow of one seems to be attracted to the shadow of the other. The experiment is illustrated by Fig. 1 and Fig. 2.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-6-5-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «ФИЗИКА» = PHYSICS; «Рис. 1: Лампа освещает линейку и книжку. На стене наблюдаются тени.» = Fig. 1: The lamp illuminates a ruler and a book. Shadows are observed on the wall.]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2020-6-5-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 2: Область «притягивающихся» теней. Фрагмент фотографии сильно увеличен.» = Fig. 2: The region of “attracting” shadows. The fragment of the photograph is greatly enlarged.]

problems.title: Problem 1: Basin on wheels
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Basin on wheels

A basin on wheels moves in the rain along a horizontal road. The total mass of raindrops per unit volume is $\rho$, and their speed near the ground is $u$. The area of the upper horizontal cross-section of the basin is $S$. At the initial moment ($t=0$) the basin is empty, its mass together with the wheels is $M$, and its speed is $v_0$ ($v_0\ll u$). Everywhere below, rolling friction and air drag may be neglected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2021-1-1-fig1.png

A. Suppose there is a small hole in the bottom of the basin. The rainwater that gets into the basin flows down to the bottom, spreads over it in a thin layer and flows out through the hole. The mass of water in the basin may be considered negligible compared with the mass of the basin.

A1) What distance $L_1$ will the basin travel before it stops if the drops fall vertically? (5 points)

A2) A headwind (for the basin) began to blow, so that the horizontal component of the velocity of the drops near the ground became $w$, and the vertical component equals $u$. What distance $L_2$ will the basin travel before it stops if the time of motion is $t$? (2 points)

B. In this part of the problem it is assumed that there are no holes in the basin, and all the rainwater that gets into the basin stays in it. During the time considered the water does not fill the basin completely and does not overflow the side. There is no wind, the velocity of the drops is vertical.

B1) Determine the dependence of the speed of the basin on time $v(t)$ in this case. (2 points)

B2) If the basin travels the distance $S$ by the moment when the mass of water in it becomes equal to the mass of the basin $M$, what distance will it travel by the moment when the mass of water in it becomes $3M$? (3 points)
