problems.title: Problem 2: Radiates and falls
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Radiates and falls

In accordance with the laws of classical electrodynamics, a charged particle moving with acceleration radiates electromagnetic waves. Relativistic effects are not taken into account in this problem. The mass and the absolute value of the charge of the electron, the speed of light in vacuum and the electric constant are equal to $m_e$, $e$, $c$ and $\varepsilon_0$ respectively.

2a. (4 points) Let an electron move around a proton along an orbit close to circular. The proton is considered stationary, since its mass is much greater than $m_e$. It is known that the power radiated by the moving electron is given by the formula
$$P=A\cdot e^{\alpha}c^{\beta}\varepsilon_0^{\gamma}a^{\delta},$$
where $a$ is the acceleration of the electron, $A$ is a dimensionless constant. Determine the exponents $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$.

2b. (6 points) In the process of radiation the energy of the electron decreases, so it must move not along a circle but along a spiral and at some moment of time must fall onto the proton. Assuming that during a time equal to the period of revolution of the electron the distance $R$ between the electron and the proton changes insignificantly, and also considering the constant $A$ in the formula above to be known, determine the time $\Delta t$ in which the distance $R$ decreases from the known value $R_0$ by $\Delta R$, provided that $\Delta R\ll R_0$. Find the time $t_{1/2}$ in which the distance $R$ decreases from the value $R_0$ to the value $\frac{R_0}{2}$.

Hint. The following formula may turn out to be useful
$$\int_a^b x^n\,dx=\frac{1}{n+1}\left(b^{n+1}-a^{n+1}\right),\qquad n\ne-1.$$

problems.title: Problem 3: Similar to a diode
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Similar to a diode

Two flat metal plates of area $S$ are located parallel to each other at the points with coordinates $x=0$ (the first plate) and $x=d$ (the second plate), and $S\gg d^2$. The axis $OX$ is perpendicular to the plates. The first plate is grounded, the potential of the second plate is $-U_0$. The space between the plates is filled with a semiconductor in which the charge carriers are particles with charge $q$ ($q>0$). The current in the semiconductor is the collective directed motion of these particles. The permittivity of the semiconductor is equal to unity. The electric constant is $\varepsilon_0$.

3a. (5 points) For large values of $U_0$ the motion of the charge carriers is determined by the action of electric forces and resistance forces. One may assume that the average velocity of the carriers in the direction of the field at the point with coordinate $x$ in the space between the plates is proportional to the field strength at this point, $v(x)=\mu E(x)$, where $\mu$ is a known constant.

Let the current between the plates be steady, the average velocity of the carriers $v(x)$, the charge density $\rho(x)$ and the potential $U(x)$ not change with time. Assuming that the potential depends on the coordinate by the power law $U(x)=Ax^{\alpha}$, determine the values of the constants $A$ and $\alpha$. Find the current between the plates. Consider the values of the parameters $U_0$, $\mu$, $d$ and $S$ to be known.

3b. (4 points) For small values of $U_0$ the motion of the carriers is due to diffusion. The current in this case satisfies the relation
$$I=-S\left(\frac{\mu kT}{q}\right)\frac{d\rho}{dx},$$
where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant, $T$ is the absolute temperature. Let the current between the plates be steady. Assuming a power-law dependence of the potential on the coordinate $U(x)=Bx^{\beta}$, determine the values of the constants $B$ and $\beta$. Find the current. Consider the values of the parameters $U_0$, $\mu$, $d$, $q$, $T$ and $S$ to be known.

3c. (2 points) What strong inequality of the form
$$U_0\ll f(q,\mu,T)$$
must the value of the potential $U_0$ satisfy so that it can be considered small, as in part 3b?

problems.title: Problem 4: Thermodynamics of a liquid
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Thermodynamics of a liquid

The coefficient of thermal expansion at constant pressure of a certain liquid is $\alpha=\frac{1}{V}\cdot\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta T}=7.5\cdot10^{-4}\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$, the compressibility of this liquid at constant temperature is $\beta=-\frac{1}{V}\cdot\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta P}=1.1\cdot10^{-9}\ \mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, and its molar heat capacity at constant volume is $c_V=112\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$. These parameters may be considered constant under the conditions of this problem. The internal energy of one mole of the liquid in question is a function of two variables, the molar volume $V$ and the temperature $T$, and is given by the formula
$$U(V,T)=A_1T+A_2V+A_3VT-pV,$$
where $A_1$, $A_2$, $A_3$ are unknown constants, $V$ is the molar volume, $p=p(V,T)$ is the molar pressure, which is a function of the same two variables $V$ and $T$.

4a. (2 points) Considering the molar volume $V$ as a function of two variables, the molar pressure $p$ and the temperature $T$, express the small change $dV$ in terms of the small changes $dp$ and $dT$ and the constants given in the statement.

4b. (2 points) Determine the dependence of the pressure on the temperature $p(T)$ in an isochoric process, assuming the value of the pressure $p_0$ at the temperature $T_0$ to be known. Express the answer in terms of the constants given in the statement and the parameters $p_0$ and $T_0$.

4c. (2 points) Find the values of the constants $A_1$ and $A_3$ in the expression for the internal energy. In this part and in the following ones obtain numerical answers.

4d. (4 points) Considering an infinitesimal Carnot cycle performed with the liquid, determine the value of the constant $A_2$ in the expression for the internal energy.

4e. (2 points) For the temperature $T_0=300\ \mathrm{K}$ determine the value of the molar heat capacity at constant pressure $c_p$, if the molar volume of the liquid in the state in question is $V=58\ \mathrm{cm^3/mol}$.

problems.title: Problem 5: Gratings
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Gratings

A diffraction grating (see the figure on the left) is an opaque plate in which $N$ ($N\gg1$) narrow slits (rulings) of thickness $h$ are made with spatial period $D$. In this problem we consider gratings containing $n=100$ rulings per millimetre, assuming that $h=0.1D$. In all parts of the problem the grating is placed parallel to the screen on which the diffraction pattern is observed, at a distance $L=3\ \mathrm{m}$ from it. The screen is a section of a vertical wall of height $1\ \mathrm{m}$ and width $2\ \mathrm{m}$. The grating is illuminated by the beam of a laser pointer of diameter $d=2\ \mathrm{mm}$ with wavelength $\lambda=532\ \mathrm{Nm}$, incident on the grating along the normal. If the grating were absent, the beam would hit the centre of the screen.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-2-5-fig1.png

5a. (5 points) Let the rulings of the grating be oriented vertically. When the laser beam is normally incident on the grating, a system of bright spots is observed on the screen. How many bright spots in total will be visible on the screen? What will the distance between neighbouring spots near the centre of the screen be? Estimate the transverse size of the central bright spot.

5b. (7 points) Let two diffraction gratings be superimposed on each other. The rulings of one grating are horizontal, and the rulings of the other make an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal line. The result is an opaque plate on which transparent regions in the form of parallelograms are periodically distributed. Such a plate is shown schematically in the figure below, the dark parallelograms symbolise the transparent regions.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-2-5-fig2.png

When such a two-dimensional grating is illuminated with a laser, a system of bright spots is observed on the screen. Let the coordinate system $YOX$ be set on the screen, the directions of the axes $OY$ and $OX$ coincide with the directions of the axes in the figure, the origin is at the centre of the screen.

Let the angle $\alpha$ be equal to $\frac{\pi}{2}$. Make a drawing, depict the diffraction pattern. Indicate the coordinates of the bright spots on the screen.

Indicate the coordinates of the bright spots for the case $\alpha\ne\frac{\pi}{2}$. Describe qualitatively the trajectory of the maxima as the angle $\alpha$ increases.

problems.title: Problem 1: What does π have to do with it?
problems.problem:
Problem 1: What does π have to do with it?

Two small blocks rest on a smooth horizontal table; their masses are $m_1=1\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $m_2=10^{N}\ \mathrm{kg}$, where $N$ is some constant. At the moment $t=0$ the second block is given a velocity $v_0$ (see the figure). The collisions of the blocks with each other and with the wall in the subsequent motion are considered perfectly elastic.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-4-1-fig1.png

Let the axis $OX$ be directed to the right, the coordinate of the wall be zero. We follow the motion of the blocks by considering the dependence $x_2(x_1)$, the coordinate of the second block at some moment of time versus the coordinate of the first block at the same moment. The position of the blocks at which their coordinates are equal to $x_1$ and $x_2$ corresponds to the point $M$ with coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$. With time the coordinates of the blocks change, and the point $M$ moves in the plane $X_1OX_2$.

1a. (2 points) Find the velocity of the point $M$ at the moment when the projections of the velocities of the blocks on the axis $OX$ are equal to $v_1$ and $v_2$ respectively. What angle does the velocity vector of the point $M$ make with the axis $OX_1$? Draw the trajectory of the point $M$ in the plane $X_1OX_2$ for the masses $m_1=m_2=1\ \mathrm{kg}$ ($N=0$).

Let us introduce the coordinates $(\tilde x_1,\tilde x_2)$ related to the coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$ by the formulas $\tilde x_1=\sqrt{m_1}\,x_1$ and $\tilde x_2=\sqrt{m_2}\,x_2$. The position of the blocks at which their coordinates are equal to $x_1$ and $x_2$ corresponds to the point $\tilde M$ with coordinates $(\tilde x_1,\tilde x_2)$ in the plane $\tilde X_1O\tilde X_2$.

1b. (4 points) Using the law of conservation of energy, show that the magnitude of the velocity of the point $\tilde M$ is conserved in a perfectly elastic collision of the blocks.

Let, an instant before the collision of the blocks, the acute angle between the line given by the equation $\tilde x_2=\frac{\sqrt{m_2}}{\sqrt{m_1}}\tilde x_1$ and the velocity of the point $\tilde M$ be equal to $\alpha$. Using the laws of conservation of momentum and energy, prove that after the collision of the blocks the acute angle between the line $\tilde x_2=\frac{\sqrt{m_2}}{\sqrt{m_1}}\tilde x_1$ and the velocity of the point $\tilde M$ is also equal to $\alpha$.

1c. (3 points) At what distance from the wall will the fifth collision of the blocks occur if the parameter $N$ is equal to $2$?

1d. (3 points) How many times will the block of mass $m_1$ collide with the block of mass $m_2$ and with the wall for $N=4$?

Hint. The approximate formula $\tan x\approx\sin x\approx x$, valid for small $x$ ($x\ll1$), may turn out to be useful.

problems.title: Problem 2: Pulling a rope
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Pulling a rope

Inside a fixed horizontal thin tube bent in the shape of a semicircle of radius $R$ there is a uniform flexible rope of length $\pi R$ whose mass is $m$. The rope is pulled by its free end $A$, applying a force tangentially, as shown in the figure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-4-2-fig1.png

What is the total reaction force of the tube acting on the rope, and in which direction is it directed, if the acceleration of the point $A$ of the rope is equal to $a$? Consider the inner walls of the tube to be smooth and the rope inextensible. Consider the initial moment of time, when the velocity of the rope is equal to zero. The force of gravity may be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 3: A gas cylinder on a platform
problems.problem:
Problem 3: A gas cylinder on a platform

A cart is placed on horizontal straight rails and can move along them without resistance. A vessel of cylindrical shape is fixed on the cart, its axis is parallel to the rails. The length of the cylinder and its radius are $L$ and $r$ respectively. The mass of the cart with the empty vessel is $M$. The vessel is filled with an ideal gas of mass $m$ at temperature $T_0$. One base of the vessel is maintained at temperature $T_0$. The temperature of the other base is also equal to $T_0$ at the initial moment, but then it is slowly increased to the value $T_0+\Delta T$ (it is known that $\Delta T\ll T_0$). The lateral surface of the vessel is thermally insulated.

Let us introduce the axis $OX$, directing it along the axis of the cylinder from the base with temperature $T_0+\Delta T$ to the base with temperature $T_0$. Let the origin coincide with the base of the cylinder with temperature $T_0+\Delta T$. Solve the problem approximately, neglecting all terms proportional to the square of the small parameter $\delta T=\frac{\Delta T}{T}$ and its higher powers. The approximate formula $(1+x)^n\approx1+nx$, valid for small $x$ ($|x|\ll1$), may be used.

3a. (4 points) Determine the dependence of the gas density in the cylinder on the coordinate $\rho(x)$.

3b. (5 points) Find the displacement $d$ of the cart relative to the initial position.

problems.title: Problem 4: Lomonosov's barometer
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Lomonosov's barometer

To measure small changes of the acceleration of free fall $\delta g$ (caused, for example, by a change of the height above sea level or by the attraction of the Moon), Mikhail Vasilyevich Lomonosov proposed to create an instrument (the universal barometer), whose design he described as follows: “Let us take a glass globe $AB$ with thick walls and an inner diameter of three inches; let us connect to it a barometric tube $BC$ of such a length that from the centre of the globe to the bend $C$ there are 28 inches; after the bend let a horizontal small tube $CP$ go, a foot or more in length, with a glass globe $S$ of a diameter of an inch; let the bore of the small tube $CP$ be $\frac{1}{4}$ of a line in diameter.” The diagram accompanying the description is given below (an enlarged figure is on sheet 3).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-4-4-fig1.png

It was supposed that mercury is poured into the instrument so that, with the tube $BC$ in the vertical position, the larger globe is half filled (with no air left above the mercury), and the tube $PC$ is filled up to the point $Q$ (the middle of $PC$). After this the small globe was sealed, and both globes were placed in special boxes filled with melting ice. It was expected that a change of the acceleration of free fall could be detected by the change of the position of the boundary of the mercury column in the horizontal tube, which was recorded with a ruler located next to the tube. The instrument was not made, probably Lomonosov's application was rejected.

4a. (4 points) Let the distance between neighbouring divisions of the ruler scale be 1 line. What minimum relative change $\frac{\delta g}{g}$ of the acceleration of free fall could be detected with the universal barometer?

$1\ \text{foot}=12\ \text{inches}$, $1\ \text{inch}=10\ \text{lines}$, $1\ \text{inch}=2.54\ \mathrm{cm}$. The density of mercury and the pressure of its saturated vapour at $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are $13.6\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$ and $0.25\ \mathrm{kPa}$ respectively.

4b. (4 points) At what minimum height above sea level could a change of the acceleration of free fall be measured with the described instrument with a relative error of no more than $20\%$? Assume that the error is determined only by the error of reading the ruler, the radius of the Earth is equal to $6400\ \mathrm{km}$.

problems.title: Problem 5: A ring and a rod
problems.problem:
Problem 5: A ring and a rod

In a uniform dielectric cylinder of length $2L$ and diameter $2R$ a cylindrical channel of small radius $r$ ($r\ll R$) coaxial with the cylinder is made (see the figure below).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-4-5-fig1.png

A uniformly charged rod of length $2L$ and circular cross-section is inserted into the channel, the diameter of the rod is slightly smaller than the diameter of the channel. The rod can move freely along the axis of the channel. A thin uniformly charged ring is fixed on the cylinder, the plane of which is perpendicular to the axis of the cylinder and divides the cylinder in half. The ring and the rod are not shown in the figure. The mass of the cylinder with the ring is equal to the mass of the rod and is equal to $M$. The rod and the ring carry equal charges of opposite signs, equal in absolute value to $q$. The rod is displaced by a small distance $x_0$ ($x_0\ll L$) from the equilibrium position and released.

5a. (4 points) What is the maximum speed of the rod if the cylinder is fixed?

5b. (2 points) What is the maximum speed of the rod after the release of the system if the cylinder is not held by an external force?

Gravity, all kinds of friction, and also the effects connected with the polarisation of the dielectric may be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 1: Frequency of ultrasound
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Frequency of ultrasound

1a. (2 points) A source of ultrasonic pulses moves along a straight line with speed $v$ towards a stationary receiver located on the same line. The source emits short pulses with frequency $f_0$. With what frequency $f$ does the receiver receive them? How will the answer change if the source moves away from the receiver? The speed of propagation of ultrasound is $c$, and $c\gg v$.

An ultrasonic detector is installed on the sea floor. A ship moves along a straight line with constant speed $v$, passing at some moment of time directly above the detector. An ultrasonic pulse source is installed on the ship, emitting pulses with frequency $f_0$ with equal intensity in any direction. The detector receives pulses with frequency $f$ different from the frequency of the emitted pulses. Denote by $n=\frac{f}{f_0}$ the ratio of these frequencies. The figure below shows a fragment of the dependence of the ratio $n$ on time as the ship moves. The speed of ultrasound in water is $1500\ \mathrm{m/s}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-6-1-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «t, 10² c» = t, 10² s; the numbers on the axes have decimal commas (1,004 = 1.004)]

1b. (8 points) What is the speed of the ship? At what depth is the detector located?

Hint. The following approximate formulas, valid for small values of $x$ ($|x|\ll1$), may turn out to be useful in solving the problem:
$$\sin x\approx x,\qquad \cos x\approx1-\frac{x^2}{2},\qquad \frac{1}{1+x}\approx1-x.$$

problems.title: Problem 2: It sank
problems.problem:
Problem 2: It sank

Some quantity of water is poured into a bottle with sufficiently thick walls and capacity $V=700\ \mathrm{mL}$. Covering the neck with a finger, the bottle is turned upside down, immersed in a bucket of water, and the hand is removed. The bottle floats, keeping the vertical position. A part of the bottle of volume $\Delta V=15\ \mathrm{mL}$ projects above the surface of the water. The bucket with the bottle is taken out of the room, in which the air temperature is $t_0=25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, into the frost. One may consider that in the course of cooling the air inside the bottle contracts, and its volume changes according to the law $V=V_0\left(1+\alpha(t-t_0)\right)$, where $V_0$ is the volume of the air at temperature $t_0$, $\alpha$ is a coefficient equal to $3.6\cdot10^{-3}\ \mathrm{1/^\circ C}$. Find the temperature of the air inside the bottle at the moment when the bottle becomes completely submerged in the water. The mass of the bottle is $300\ \mathrm{g}$, the density of the material of which it is made is $\rho=2600\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the density of water is $\rho_0=1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$.

Problem 4: Collisions on a plane

Two absolutely identical blocks are held at a distance $L=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ from each other on a sufficiently extended inclined plane making an angle $\alpha=30^\circ$ with the horizontal. At the moment $t=0$ the blocks are released and begin to move. The quantities relating to the block that is the upper one at the initial moment are marked below with the index 1, and those relating to the lower one with the index 2. Denote by $v_1(t)$ and $v_2(t)$ the velocities of the blocks at the moment $t$. The coefficients of friction against the plane are $\mu_1=\frac{\sqrt3}{6}$ and $\mu_2=\frac{\sqrt3}{3}$. problems.title: Problem 5: Determine from the photograph

Problem 5: Determine from the photograph

In the stroboscopic photograph (see the figure) one can see the positions, at different moments of time, of a ball moving in the gravitational field of the Earth and colliding with a horizontal surface. The time intervals between two successive flashes of the stroboscopic lamp are equal. The photograph is inverted (black colour is changed to white, white is replaced by black), the grid was superimposed in a graphics editor later for convenience of calculations. The collisions of the ball with the horizontal surface cannot be considered elastic; in the process of collision the kinetic energy of translational motion of the ball decreases.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2023-6-5-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 1: Potential graph

Problem 1: Potential graph

Three identical thin discs of radius $R$, uniformly charged with surface charge densities $\sigma$, $2\sigma$ and $-3\sigma$, are placed so that the axis $OX$ is the common axis of the discs, and the centres of the discs are at the points with coordinates $0$, $d$ and $2d$, where $d=\frac{R}{1000}$. The potential at the centre of an isolated disc uniformly charged with surface density $\sigma$ is $1000\ \mathrm{V}$. The potential of a point infinitely far away is taken to be zero.

a) (2 points) Derive the formula $\varphi_0=\frac{\sigma R}{2\varepsilon_0}$ giving the potential at the centre of an isolated uniformly charged disc. This formula may be used in the next part, even if you cannot derive it.

Problem 2: Air hockey

a) (2 points) At the initial moment pucks 2, 3, 4, 5 are placed so that their centres are the vertices of a square (see figure); puck 1 hits puck 2 with speed $v=1\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Find the velocities of the pucks after all collisions have ceased.

Problem 3: With two batteries

In the circuit whose diagram is shown in the figure below, the parameters $\mathcal{E}$, $L$, $C$ are known. The resistance of the connecting wires and of the coil is zero. The internal resistance of the battery $r$ and the resistance of the resistor $R$ satisfy the relations
$$r\ll R,\qquad rC\ll\sqrt{LC},\qquad RC=\sqrt{2LC}.$$

Initially the switch (labelled «П» in the figure) is in position 1, and a steady state has been established in the circuit. The voltage across the capacitor connected to terminal 2 is zero. At time $t=0$ the switch is instantly moved to position 2.

problems.title: Problem 4: Pumping up a tire
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Pumping up a tire

The problem considers a physical model describing some features of the process of inflating a bicycle wheel inner tube. The volume of the tube $V_0$ is considered constant. The initial air pressure in the tube is $P_0$ at ambient temperature $T_0$. After inflation the air in the tube must produce pressure $P$ at the same temperature $T_0$. The air is considered an ideal diatomic gas ($c_V=2.5R$).

a) (6 points) In this part the tube is connected through the valve (nipple) to a vessel of very large volume $V_1$ ($V_1\gg V_0$), which contains air at temperature $T_0$ and at such a pressure $P_{\max}$ ($P_{\max}>P$) that after the tube is filled and cooled to temperature $T_0$ the air pressure in the tube becomes equal to $P$. The nipple lets air into the tube until the pressure in it equals the pressure in the vessel; after that the nipple closes and does not let air back out.

The “pushing” of a portion of air from the vessel into the tube occurs very quickly, so it may be considered that the “pushing” process takes place without heat exchange between this portion and the air remaining in the vessel, and also between the air in the tube and the environment. As a result the temperature and pressure of the air in the tube rise to the values $P_{\max}$ and $T_{\max}$. Some time after that the temperature of the air in the tube becomes equal to the ambient temperature $T_0$, and the pressure in the tube becomes equal to $P$.

Assuming the values $T_0=300\ \mathrm{K}$, $P=3\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $P_0=10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$ to be known, determine $P_{\max}$ and $T_{\max}$.

b) Now imagine that the tube is inflated with a hand pump. At the beginning of each cycle the pump cylinder of volume $V_C$ ($V_C\ll V_0$) is filled with air at atmospheric pressure $P_0$ and temperature $T_0$. Let the pressure in the tube at the beginning of the $i$-th cycle be $P_{i-1}$. In the $i$-th cycle the air in the cylinder is first adiabatically compressed by the piston from pressure $P_0$ to pressure $P_i$, and then “pushed” through the nipple at constant pressure $P_i$ without heat exchange, as in part a) of the problem. After that the inlet valve opens, through which air from the environment at pressure $P_0$ enters the pump cylinder, the piston moves back to its initial position, and the cylinder is filled with atmospheric air at pressure $P_0$. This ends the cycle. Naturally, one will have to perform quite many ($N\gg1$) such cycles of “pushing” air into the tube so that, after the temperature $T_0$ is established, the pressure in the tube becomes equal to $P$. Since the inflation of the tube proceeds very quickly, heat exchange between the air in the tube and the environment begins only after the pump has finished working.

b1) (1 point) How many cycles $N$ must be performed to inflate the tube? The parameters $P_0$, $P$, $V_C$ and $V_0$ are considered known.

b2) (3 points) What work $A_i$ does the piston perform in the $i$-th cycle? Express the answer in terms of $P_0$, $P_i$ and $V_C$.

b3) (2 points) Determine the change of pressure in the tube $\Delta P_i$ in the $i$-th cycle, considering $P_0$, $P_i$, $V_C$ and $V_0$ to be known.

b4) (2 points) To find the pressure in the tube after the end of the $k$-th cycle, we use the following device. The relation obtained in the previous part can be represented in the form
$$\frac{\Delta P_i}{f(P_i)}=\alpha,\tag{1}$$
where $f(P_i)$ is some function of $P_i$, and $\alpha$ is a coefficient independent of $P_i$ ($\alpha$ and $f(P_i)$ are known to you if you have done part b3). Let us sum the expressions given by formula (1) from $i=1$ to $i=k$:
$$\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{\Delta P_i}{f(P_i)}=\alpha\cdot k.\tag{2}$$
The summation in formula (1) can be approximately replaced by integration:
$$\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{\Delta P_i}{f(P_i)}\approx\int_{P_0}^{P_k}\frac{dP}{f(P)}.$$
Determine the pressure $P_k$ in the tube after the $k$-th cycle. The parameters $P_0$, $V_C$, $V_0$ and $k$ are considered known.

b5) (1 point) Calculate $P_{\max}$ and $T_{\max}$, assuming the values of the parameters $T_0=300\ \mathrm{K}$, $P=3\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $P_0=10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$ to be known.

Hint. The value of a definite integral of a power function is given by the formula
$$\int_{a_1}^{a_2}\frac{dx}{x^{k}}=\frac{1}{(k-1)}\left(\frac{1}{a_1^{k-1}}-\frac{1}{a_2^{k-1}}\right).$$

problems.title: Problem 5: Cylindrical lens
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Cylindrical lens

If a cylinder of glass with refractive index $n$ is cut by a plane parallel to the axis of the cylinder, a cylindrical segment results, which from the optical point of view is a cylindrical lens. If the thickness $h$ of this lens (see figure) is small compared with its width $L$ and the radius of curvature $R$ of the convex surface, one can speak of a thin cylindrical lens. For such a lens the transverse magnification has different values in different directions. In the direction along the axis $O$ the transverse magnification equals $1$; in other words, the sizes of the object and of the image along this axis are the same. We call axis $O$ the straight line parallel to the axis of the original cylinder and passing through the midpoint of the chord $A_1A_2$ (see figure).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-1-5-fig1.png

a) (3 points) Let a parallel beam of light of circular cross-section fall on the flat side of a thin cylindrical lens. The axis of the beam is perpendicular to the flat surface of the lens and intersects the axis $O$ of the lens. The radii of the beam and of the convex surface of the lens are $r$ and $R$ respectively, and the refractive index of the lens material is $n=\frac{4}{3}$. Behind the lens, at a distance $2R$ from it, there is a screen parallel to the plane of the lens. Determine the area of the bright spot on the screen. All rays of the beam pass through the lens.

b) (7 points) A thin-walled measuring beaker of diameter $80\ \mathrm{mm}$ (the thickness of the walls may be neglected) is filled with water (refractive index $1.33$) and stands on a horizontal table at an unknown distance from a vertical wall. A sheet on which three parallel straight lines are drawn is fixed on the wall. They are observed through the beaker. Using the photograph given below (an enlarged version is on the additional sheet), determine the distance from the axis of the beaker to the wall.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-1-5-fig2.png

problems.title: Problem 5: Compressing saturated vapor
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Compressing saturated vapor

In a heat-conducting cylinder under a piston, at the ambient temperature $T_0$, there is one mole of saturated water vapor. There is no liquid water in the vessel. The universal gas constant and the molar mass of water are $R=8.3\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$ and $\mu=18\ \mathrm{g/mol}$. The density of liquid water is $1\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$.

A. (2 points) Let the volume under the piston be decreased very slowly by $10\%$ at constant temperature $T_0$. Neglecting the volume of the liquid water that forms, determine the work of the external forces acting on the piston $A_{\mathrm{ext}}^{(T)}$, and also the change of the internal energy of the contents of the vessel $\Delta U^{(T)}$. The specific heat of vaporization of water is $L$. In this part of the problem the answer is expected in general form.

The dependence of the saturated vapor pressure on temperature in a certain range of temperatures is given in the tables presented below. The values given in these tables may be considered known in all the following parts of the problem.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline t,\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}&23&24&25&26&27&28&29&30\\\hline p,\ \mathrm{kPa}&2.81&2.99&3.17&3.36&3.57&3.78&4.01&4.25\\\hline\end{array}$$
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline t,\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}&31&32&33&34&35&36&37&38\\\hline p,\ \mathrm{kPa}&4.50&4.76&5.03&5.32&5.63&5.95&6.28&6.63\\\hline\end{array}$$

B. (2 points) Determine the value of the specific heat of vaporization $L$ at a temperature of $27\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

C. (3 points) Let the state of a mole of saturated water vapor taken at a temperature of $27\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}$ change in such a way that the vapor remains saturated all the time, while its volume decreases by $10\%$. Determine the work of the external forces acting on the piston $A_{\mathrm{ext}}^{(\mathrm{sat})}$, and also the change of the internal energy of the contents of the vessel $\Delta U^{(\mathrm{sat})}$ in this case.

D. (4 points) Imagine that the volume of a mole of saturated vapor taken at a temperature of $27\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}$ decreases by $10\%$ adiabatically. Find the work of the external forces acting on the piston $A_{\mathrm{ext}}^{(Q)}$, and also the change of the internal energy of the contents of the vessel $\Delta U^{(Q)}$ for this case.

Hint. On the saturation line the Clapeyron–Clausius equation holds
$$\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{L}{T\left(\frac{1}{\rho_{\mathrm{g}}}-\frac{1}{\rho_{\mathrm{l}}}\right)},$$
where $dP$ and $dT$ are the changes of pressure and temperature on the saturation line, $L$ is the specific heat of vaporization, $\rho_{\mathrm{g}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{l}}$ are the density of the gas phase and the density of the liquid phase near the saturation line at temperature $T$.

problems.title: Problem 1: Rod on a plane
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Rod on a plane

A uniform rod of mass $m$ moves in a plane so that at some moment of time the magnitudes of the accelerations of the ends $A$ and $B$ of the rod are $a_A=2a_0$ and $a_B=a_0$, the accelerations being directed along parallel straight lines, and the velocity vectors of the ends are equal to each other. What external force acts on the rod at this moment? Determine the magnitude and direction of the force vector.

problems.title: Problem 2: Thermodynamic cycle
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Thermodynamic cycle

The state of one mole of an ideal diatomic gas changes in a cycle consisting of processes with constant heat capacity. The figure below shows the graph of the work done by the gas versus the amount of heat received or given up by it on reaching the current state.

A. (3 points) Determine the efficiency of the cycle.

B. (3 points) What is the minimum temperature of the gas in this cyclic process if the maximum temperature is $481\ \mathrm{K}$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-4-2-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «A, кДж» = A, kJ; «Q, кДж» = Q, kJ; decimal commas on the scale]

Note. A quasi-static process in which the molar heat capacity $c$ of the gas remains constant is described by the relation
$$PV^{\frac{c-c_P}{c-c_V}}=\mathrm{const},$$
where $P$ and $V$ are the pressure and volume respectively, and $c_V$ and $c_P=c_V+R$ are the molar heat capacities at constant volume and at constant pressure.

problems.title: Problem 3: A monkey pulls a boa constrictor
problems.problem:
Problem 3: A monkey pulls a boa constrictor

The boa constrictor has straightened out, lying on a horizontal surface, has relaxed and does not resist at all. Its mass $M$ is uniformly distributed along its length $L$. The surface is smooth, and next to the boa constrictor and parallel to it a (not smooth) path for walks has been laid. The monkey, standing on this path, grabbed the boa constrictor by the tip of its tail and pulled this end of the boa towards its head. The boa constrictor lies entirely on the surface. The force $F$ with which the monkey pulls the tail of the boa is horizontal and varies depending on the time $t$ according to the law $F=At$, where $A$ is a known constant.

A. (4 points) At what speed was the tip of the boa's tail moving at the moment when the distance from it to the boa's head first became equal to $\frac{L}{2}$?

B. (2 points) After what time will the boa's tail come level with the stationary head of the boa?

C. (2 points) What will be the speed of the whole boa at the moment when its head starts to move?

Hint. The following formula may turn out to be useful:
$$\int_a^b x^n\,dx=\frac{1}{n+1}\left(b^{n+1}-a^{n+1}\right),\qquad n\neq-1.$$

problems.title: Problem 4: Differences
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Differences

Two identical flat dielectric plates, uniformly charged over the surface with densities $\sigma$ and $-\sigma$, are placed parallel to each other at a small distance $h$ (see figure). Each plate has the shape of a rhombus with acute angle $\alpha$ ($\frac{\pi}{6}\leqslant\alpha\leqslant\frac{\pi}{3}$) and side length $a$ ($a\gg h$). Any vertex of the upper plate and the nearest vertex of the lower plate lie on a common perpendicular to the planes of the plates.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-4-4-fig1.png

A. (1 point) Find the potential difference between the centres of the plates. The centre of a rhombus is taken to be the point of intersection of its diagonals.

B. (2 points) Determine the potential difference between the midpoints of the nearest sides of the plates (points $B_1$ and $B_2$).

C. (3 points) What is the potential difference between the vertices $A_1$ and $A_2$ of the rhombi? And the potential difference between the vertices $C_1$ and $C_2$?

problems.title: Problem 5: Tilt-Shift
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Tilt-Shift

The design of a photographic tilt-shift lens allows the optical axis of the lens to be tilted and shifted relative to the line of sight (the line connecting the camera and the object being photographed). Tilting the optical axis makes it possible to obtain sharp images of extended objects whose different points are at different distances from the camera.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-4-5-fig1.png

In the simplified diagram shown in the figure, the converging lens $L$ represents the lens (objective). The principal optical axis of the lens $oo_1$ is deflected by an angle $\varphi$ from the line of sight $AA_1$, which makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal. The photographed object is represented by the segment $BC$; $pp_1$ is the plane in which the light-sensitive sensor of the camera (or the film, in the case of a film camera) is located.

Let the horizontal distance $AB=5\ \mathrm{m}$ between the camera sensor and the object, the focal length of the lens $f=50\ \mathrm{mm}$, and also the angle $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}$ between the line of sight and the horizontal be known. The angle $\varphi$ of rotation of the principal optical axis is chosen so that all points of the luminous segment $BC$ are imaged in the plane $pp_1$ of the camera sensor as sharply as possible. Find the angle $\varphi$, assuming it is small.

Hint. For a small angle $\beta$ ($|\beta|\ll1$) the following approximate relations hold:
$$\sin\beta\approx\beta,\qquad \tan\beta\approx\beta,\qquad \cos\beta\approx1.$$

The velocity of the axis of the hoop and the frequency of its revolution around this axis, equal to one revolution per second, do not change with time. A small lamp is fixed at some point of the hoop, flashing brightly at equal intervals of time with a frequency of 4 times per second. In a photograph taken from above with a long exposure, with the proportions of the depicted objects preserved, one can see the positions of the lamp during successive flashes. problems.title: Problem 2: Both rest and sliding
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Both rest and sliding

Studying the friction force within the school physics course, one usually says that the maximum value of the force of static friction is equal to the force of sliding friction. In fact, to bring a body out of the state of rest, one needs to apply a force somewhat greater than the force of sliding friction. Therefore it makes sense to speak of two coefficients: the coefficient of static friction $\mu_r$ and the coefficient of sliding friction $\mu_s$ ($\mu_s<\mu_r$). The force of static friction satisfies the relation $F_{\mathrm{fr.st}}\leqslant\mu_rN$. After the transition to sliding, another coefficient is used to determine the friction force: $F_{\mathrm{fr.sl}}=\mu_sN$.

A. (4 points) For a wooden block of mass $m$ located on an extended wooden horizontal surface, the coefficients of static and sliding friction are $\mu_r=0.5$ and $\mu_s=0.4$ respectively. A periodically varying horizontal force begins to act on the block; its projection on the horizontal axis $OX$ during the first half of the period is $F_x^{(1)}=1.001\,\mu_rmg$, and during the second half of the period it changes sign and becomes $F_x^{(2)}=-1.001\,\mu_rmg$. Plot the dependence of the speed of the block on time during two periods, a long time after the beginning of the process. The period of change of the force is $T=4\ \mathrm{s}$, the acceleration of free fall is $10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

B. (5 points) Two boards of equal mass $m$ lie on each other and on a long horizontal wooden table (see figure). The coefficients of static and sliding friction between all surfaces are $\mu_r=0.5$ and $\mu_s=0.4$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-6-2-fig1.png

B1) (2 points) An external horizontal force $F(t)$ directly proportional to time, $F(t)=\frac{\mu_rmgt}{t_0}$, acts on the upper board. Plot the dependence of the acceleration of the upper board on time for $t\in[0,4t_0]$.

B2) (3 points) Now let the external horizontal force $F(t)=\frac{\mu_rmgt}{t_0}$ act on the lower board. Plot the dependence of the acceleration of the lower board on time for $t\in[0,4t_0]$.

In both cases the boards are initially at rest. In the course of the motion one board does not fall off the other.

problems.title: Problem 3: Freezing drops
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Freezing drops

In a temperature inversion, the graph of the dependence of the air temperature $t$ near the Earth's surface on the height $h$ can have the form shown in the figure by the black line of increased thickness.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-6-3-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «h, км» = h, km; «t, °C» = t, °C; decimal commas on the scale]

Let a drop, having the shape of a sphere, move downward at constant speed under the action of gravity and of the air drag force. At a height $h_0=2\ \mathrm{km}$ the temperature of the drop turns out to be $t_c=0\ {}^\circ\mathrm{C}$. In the course of its further fall part of the drop (or the whole drop) turns into ice owing to heat exchange with the cold atmospheric air.

The power of heat exchange $P$ and the air drag force $F_d$ are given by the formulas
$$P=\alpha(t_c-t)S,\qquad F_d=\beta Sv^2,$$
where $S$ is the surface area of the drop, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are some constants, $t$ and $t_c$ are the temperatures of the surrounding air and of the drop (at the same height), and $v$ is the speed of the drop.

Consider two drops. The radius of the first drop is 2.25 times smaller than that of the second. In the course of falling from a height of $2\ \mathrm{km}$, a quarter of the mass of the first drop turns into ice. What fraction of the mass of the second drop will turn into ice?

Assume that the thermal conductivity of ice is high, so that the temperature of all points of the drop remains the same until the drop has completely turned into ice. The change of the radius of the drop upon its partial transformation into ice may be neglected.

problems.title: Problem 4: Circuits with a tunnel diode

The currents and voltages $I_1$, $I_2$, $U_1$ and $U_2$ marked on the graph will be called the parameters of the diode. The angles marked on the graph are considered equal.

This diode was connected to an ideal source with voltage $U_0=6u$ in series with a variable resistor whose resistance can vary over wide limits (see the figure presented below). For what values of the resistance of the resistor is the value of the current in the circuit determined uniquely?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2024-6-4-fig2.png

B. (5 points) The parameters of another tunnel diode are $I_1=1\ \mathrm{mA}$, $I_2=10\ \mathrm{mA}$, $U_1=0.2\ \mathrm{V}$, $U_2=0.8\ \mathrm{V}$. Using this diode and a ballast resistor $R_0$, a circuit was assembled according to the diagram shown in the figure.

B2) (3 points) What can the resistance of the load $R$ be equal to? Indicate the limits of the range of possible values $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$.

problems.title: Problem 1: Establishing equilibrium
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Establishing equilibrium

In a thermally insulated cylinder placed horizontally, a light piston that conducts heat well divides the volume into two equal parts, each of volume $V_0$. Both parts contain the same monatomic ideal gas at the initial pressure $p_0$ and at temperatures $2T_0$ and $T_0$ (see the figure). The heat capacity of the piston may be neglected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-2-1-fig1.png

The power of heat exchange between the parts of the cylinder is proportional to the temperature difference: $P=\alpha(T_1-T_2)$, where $\alpha$ is the heat transfer coefficient, $T_1$ is the temperature in the left part, $T_2$ in the right part. In the process of establishing equilibrium the piston moves slowly, without friction against the walls of the cylinder.

a) (2 points) Find the final temperature of the contents of the cylinder.

b) (2 points) Find the time during which the temperature difference between the parts of the cylinder decreases by a factor of $e$ compared with the initial temperature difference $T_0$.

c) (2 points) Find the dependence of the volume of the left part of the cylinder on time, $V_1(t)$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Oscillations of a bead
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Oscillations of a bead

A bead of mass $m$ and charge $q$, charged with the same sign as the ring, rests at the lowest point of a smooth, uniformly charged semicircular ring of radius $R$ fixed in a vertical plane. The linear charge density of the semicircle is $\lambda$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-2-2-fig1.png

b) (3 points) Let the charge $q$ of the bead be such that its equilibrium position at the lowest point of the semicircle is stable. Determine the period of small oscillations of the bead near the equilibrium position. The parameters $\lambda$, $q$, $g$, $R$ and $m$ are known.

a) (2 points) The wire structure considered in this part is a ring of radius $r$. At points 1, 2 and 3, located at equal distances from one another (see Fig. 1), sources of EMF are connected to the ring, so that if the potential of point 3 is taken to be zero, the potentials of points 1 and 2 turn out to be $\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_2$ respectively. Determine the magnetic induction produced at the centre of the ring by the section 1-2.

The black dots mark the junction points. At point $A$ there is no contact between the wires. The radii of the concentric wire rings are $r$ and $2r$, the angles between the straight wire sections are equal to $\alpha$, as shown in the figure. problems.title: Problem 4: Newton's reflecting telescope
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Newton's reflecting telescope

The Newtonian reflector is a mirror analogue of the Keplerian refracting telescope. A concave spherical mirror $M_1$ (see the figure below), which is the objective of the reflecting telescope, forms a real image of a celestial body in the focal plane. This image is viewed through the eyepiece $L$, whose role is played by a converging lens. The figure also shows a flat turning mirror $M_2$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-2-4-fig1.png

The mirror deflects the converging beam reflected (from the concave mirror) to the side. The figure schematically shows the path of the rays.

a) (4 points) Let the radius of the spherical mirror be $R$ and the focal length of the lens be $F$. What is the angular magnification of the instrument?

Hint. The angular magnification $\gamma$ of optical instruments intended for observing distant objects is the ratio $\gamma=\dfrac{\alpha'}{\alpha}$, where $\alpha'$ is the angle at which the observed object is seen in the eyepiece, and $\alpha$ is the angle of view with the unaided eye from the same distance.

b) (3 points) One of the largest telescopes in the world, at the Special Astrophysical Observatory of the Russian Academy of Sciences (built according to the Newtonian design), has an objective focal length $F=300\ \mathrm{m}$. What is the maximum permissible angle $\varphi_{\max}$ of swaying of the telescope, caused by vibrations of the observatory foundation, at which the resolving power of photographic film $\delta=50$ lines/mm is still fully used when photographing astronomical objects? When photographing, the film is placed in the focal plane of the objective, and a long exposure of up to several minutes is used.

c) (3 points) Suppose that, because of construction work going on near the observatory, the telescope oscillates with an amplitude of $10^{-6}\ \mathrm{rad}$. What will be the size of the image on the film if the angular size of the source is $10^{-7}\ \mathrm{rad}$?

problems.title: Problem 5: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
problems.problem:
Problem 5: The Leaning Tower of Pisa

A metal strip bent into a spiral can be used as a torsion spring, that is, a spring that resists the rotation of mechanisms (see Fig. 3). When one tries to straighten or twist such a spring, it develops a restoring torque $M$ proportional to the angle of rotation $\alpha$: $M=\gamma\alpha$, where $\gamma$ is the constant torsional stiffness coefficient of the spring. The lower end of a light rigid vertical rod of length $l$ is rigidly attached to the free end of the torsion spring. The inner end of the spring is fixed. A force $F$ directed vertically downward is applied to the upper end of the rod.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-2-5-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 3» = Fig. 3; «Рис. 4» = Fig. 4]

a) (3 points) At what maximum force $F_{\max}$ will the vertical equilibrium position of the rod still remain stable?

b) (2 points) What will the angle of deflection be if the applied force is $F=1.01F_{\max}$?

The Leaning Tower of Pisa is one of the best-known architectural monuments. The tower is distinguished by the fact that its axis is deflected by some angle from the vertical because of the softness of the soil under its foundation. Let us consider a model of a tower standing on the ground. The tower is a uniform cylinder of height $L$ and diameter $d$ (Fig. 4); the mass per unit length of the tower is $\lambda$. The tower is placed centrally on a rigid massless square base with side $a$, to which a foam-rubber cushion of the same cross-section is glued from below. The height of the cushion, after the tower has been placed on it, is $H$. The whole construction is set on a rigid table. The mass is distributed uniformly over the tower. The Young's modulus of the foam rubber is $E$. The coefficient of friction between the tower and the base may be considered large enough that the tower does not slip relative to the base.

c) (4 points) At what minimum height $L_1$ of the tower will it take up a stable tilted position?

d) (3 points) At what minimum height $L_2$ of the tower will it topple over? Express the answer in terms of $L_1$ and $d$, assuming $d\ll L_1$.

Hint 1. For a small relative deformation $\varepsilon=\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}$ of tension/compression of a rod of cross-sectional area $S$, the elastic force arising in it can be calculated by the formula $F=E\varepsilon S$, where $E$ is the Young's modulus of the rod material.

Hint 2. In answering the questions of different parts of the problem, the approximate formulas valid for small values of $\alpha$ ($\alpha\ll1$) may prove very useful:
$$\sin\alpha\approx\alpha-\frac{\alpha^3}{6},\quad \tan\alpha\approx\alpha+\frac{\alpha^3}{3}.$$

A wheel of radius $R=50\ \mathrm{cm}$ moves without slipping over a horizontal surface, its axle moving with acceleration $a=1\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Problem 2: F-acceleration

An F-shaped tube is completely filled with mercury, as shown in the figure. The length of each arm of the tube is $L=\dfrac{p_0}{3\rho g}$, where $p_0$ is the atmospheric pressure, $\rho$ is the density of mercury, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. The tube is set into horizontal motion with a smoothly increasing acceleration $a$ (see the figure). The cross-sectional area $S$ of the tube is small ($\sqrt S\ll L$). The vapour pressure of mercury may be neglected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-4-2-fig1.png

a) (2 points) Determine the volume of mercury that has spilled out of the tube when the acceleration becomes equal to $g$. What is the pressure of the mercury at the left end of the horizontal part of the tube at that moment?

problems.title: Problem 3: A shell on the scales
problems.problem:
Problem 3: A shell on the scales

A shell with thin, poorly heat-conducting walls made of inextensible flexible polyethylene was weighed when there was no air in it, and a mass value $M=5\ \mathrm{g}$ was obtained. Then, using a pump, through a tube of small cross-section $S=0.2\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, in a very short time $\tau=5\ \mathrm{s}$ the shell was filled to a volume $V=10$ litres with air taken from outside, and the resulting bag of air was immediately weighed on the same scales. The value $0.95M$ was obtained. After a long time, when thermal equilibrium had been established, the weighing result for the shell with air again turned out to be $M$. The air pressure inside the shell and outside it is always $p_0=10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Find the temperature $T_0$ of the surrounding air.

problems.title: Problem 4: Triangle-star
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Triangle-star

It is known that any circuit with three output terminals consisting of ideal voltage sources and resistors can be represented in the form of a star or a triangle, in whose branches there are ideal power sources and resistances.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-4-4-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 1» = Fig. 1; «Рис. 2» = Fig. 2]

Let the resistances and the voltage of the source be known in the circuit in Fig. 1. Carry out an equivalent replacement of the circuit shown in Fig. 1 by the circuit shown in Fig. 2. To do this, calculate what the resistances of the resistors and the voltages of the power sources in the equivalent circuit may be. State whether such a solution will be unique. Justify your answer.

problems.title: Problem 5: Refractometer
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Refractometer

Refractometry is one of the most convenient ways of determining the concentration of impurities in a liquid by measuring its refractive index.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-4-5-fig1.png

The simplest refractometer is a tube (see the figure above), at one end of which there is a prism with a polished bevelled face. A drop of the liquid under study is applied to this face and is then pressed against the surface by a diffuser. The diffuser provides illumination of the liquid at all angles. At the other end of the tube there is an eyepiece. When one looks through the eyepiece with bright light directed onto the diffuser, a scale is seen, part of which is illuminated and part is not. The boundary between the illuminated and unilluminated regions determines the refractive index of the liquid, which is uniquely related to the concentration of impurities.

The principal optical scheme of the refractometer is shown in the figure below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-4-5-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «Собирающая линза» = converging lens; «Линза окуляра» = eyepiece lens; «Рассеиватель» = diffuser; «Исследуемая жидкость» = liquid under study; «Зачернённая поверхность» = blackened surface; «Полупрозрачный экран со шкалой» = semitransparent screen with a scale]

Behind the prism, inside the tube, there is a converging lens. In its focal plane there is a semitransparent matte screen with a scale, viewed through the eyepiece. In the simplest variant the eyepiece is a single lens, and the screen is located in its focal plane. Reflection of light from the blackened surface of the prism is assumed to be absent.

Suppose that one needs to design a refractometer for measuring the volume concentration of alcohol in water with a measurement limit of 60%. The prism of the refractometer is made of glass with refractive index $n=1.500$.

a) (3 points) What is the angle $\beta$ at the apex of the prism if, when a 30% alcohol solution with refractive index $n_{30}=1.350$ is placed on the bevelled face of the prism, the boundary of the illuminated region on the screen crosses the optical axis of the lens?

b) (4 points) Calculate the length $d$ of the scale (see the figure) on the semitransparent screen. The focal length of the lens is $F=10\ \mathrm{cm}$. The refractive index of pure water is $n=1.333$, of a 60% alcohol solution $n_{60}=1.362$.

c) (3 points) The scale of the refractometer must have a division value of 1%. Assume that the human eye comfortably distinguishes objects at a great distance if the angular distance between them is not less than $\varphi=15'$ (15 arcminutes). Calculate the maximum possible focal length $F_{\max}$ of the eyepiece.

problems.title: Problem 1: The PSR B1937+21 clock
problems.problem:
Problem 1: The PSR B1937+21 clock

In modern metrology the reference instrument for measuring time is the atomic clock. A promising alternative to atomic clocks may be pulsars, rapidly rotating neutron stars. Some pulsars have remarkable stability of rotation, emitting at each revolution of the star (at equal intervals of time) radio signals that can be registered on Earth. The pulsar PSR B1937+21 is a bright example of this.

The rotation period of the pulsar PSR B1937+21 is $T=1.557806449\ \mathrm{ms}$, the initial error of measurement of this value is $\Delta T_0=5\cdot10^{-12}\ \mathrm{s}$. The rotation rate of the pulsar may change slightly because of internal processes in the star. To take this factor into account, we assume that the error of the pulsar period increases linearly with time: $\Delta T(t)=\Delta T_0+\alpha t$, where $\alpha=7\cdot10^{-21}$ is the rate of change of the error. Suppose that a clock based on the pulsar is used to measure a long time interval $t$. At what value of $t$ will the accumulated measurement error become equal to 1 second? Assume that the mean value of the rotation period of the pulsar is constant and equal to $T$. Express the answer in years.

problems.title: Problem 2: Off-centre impact
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Off-centre impact

Two identical pucks of mass $m$, connected by an inextensible light thread, move over a horizontal smooth surface with speed $v$, as shown in the figure below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-6-2-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Гвоздь» = nail]

The thread neither sags nor is taut. In the course of the motion the thread runs onto the nail. The lengths of the segments of the thread between the pucks and the nail are $l$ and $L$. There is no friction between the thread and the nail.

a) (5 points) Find the tension of the thread immediately after the thread touches the nail, and also the acceleration of the point of the thread in contact with the nail at that moment.

b) (2 points) Determine the radii of curvature of the trajectories of the pucks at the moment when the thread touches the nail.

problems.problem:
Problem 3: A paper cone

A cone of mass $m$ with an apex angle $2\alpha$ has been rolled from a sheet of paper in the shape of a sector of a circle. The cone is placed on the horizontal surface of a table; the paper does not sag. There is no friction between the paper and the table. So that the cone does not fall apart under the action of gravity, a pair of forces of magnitude $F$, directed tangentially to the circle of the base of the cone (see the figure below), is applied to the edges of the paper located on the line of the cut. Consider the mass to be distributed uniformly over the sheet. Neglecting all effects associated with bending, find the value of the force $F$.

problems.title: Problem 4: Cooling of the broth
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Cooling of the broth

A schoolboy studied the cooling of liquids in a thermos. He found that the cooling of one litre of broth from $95\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $90\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in an open thermos takes $t_1=100\ \mathrm{s}$, and in one covered with thin foil, $t_2=180\ \mathrm{s}$. On the other hand, he noticed that water of the same volume cools from $95\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $90\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in an open thermos in $t_3=80\ \mathrm{s}$. Assume that the cooling of a liquid occurs owing to the evaporation of water and the convection of the air adjacent to its surface. At the same time, part of the surface of the broth is covered with fat, and evaporation from this part of the surface does not occur. If the broth is covered with foil, evaporation practically stops. In the temperature range under consideration the heat losses may be considered constant; the foil and the fat layer on the surface have no significant effect on the heat losses carried out by convection.

The heat capacity and the density of the broth and of water coincide. The specific heat capacity and the specific heat of vaporisation of water are, respectively, $c=4200\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot{}^\circ C)}$ and $L=2.3\ \mathrm{MJ/kg}$.

a) (3 points) Calculate what part of the surface area of the broth is covered with fat.

b) (3 points) Calculate what mass of water evaporated from the surface of the broth during its cooling from $95\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $90\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

problems.title: Problem 5: The Thomson bridge
problems.problem:
Problem 5: The Thomson bridge

One of the problems in measuring small resistances is the relatively large resistance of the lead wires and of the contacts of these wires with the resistance being measured. Let us describe such a small resistance $R$, together with the total resistance $r$ of the lead wires (including the contact resistances), by the simplest equivalent circuit shown in Fig. 1.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-6-5-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 1» = Fig. 1]

Thus, for example, when two small resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ are compared by means of a Wheatstone bridge circuit (the circuit in Fig. 2), an error arises that is connected with the presence of contact resistance.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-6-5-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 2» = Fig. 2]

To eliminate this error, William Thomson proposed a more complicated scheme for comparing resistances (see Fig. 3), which later acquired the name "Thomson bridge".

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2025-6-5-fig3.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 3» = Fig. 3]

a) (3 points) Calculate the resistance $R_1$ in the circuit in Fig. 3 if the voltage registered by the voltmeter is equal to zero (the bridge is balanced). Consider the other resistances, including the resistance of the lead wires, to be known.

b) (3 points) At what relation between the resistances $R_3$, $R_4$, $R_5$, $R_6$ does the answer to the first question not depend on $r$?

c) (2 points) Technically it is most convenient to choose the resistances $R_3$, $R_4$, $R_5$, $R_6$ much larger than the resistances $R_1$, $R_2$ and the resistance $r$ of the lead wires. Give the answer to the question of part a) with this approximation taken into account (rounding the answer to the first order of smallness).

problems.title: Problem 1: Inelastic collisions
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Inelastic collisions

In the theory of impact, a collision of bodies is characterised by the coefficient of restitution $e$. It equals the ratio of the magnitudes of the projections of the relative velocity of the contact points onto the common normal after and before the impact. In this problem $e$ is assumed to depend only on the material of the bodies.

A small smooth puck of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ collides with a dumbbell made of two identical smooth pucks, each of mass $nm$. The pucks are joined by a rigid massless rod. In an impact perpendicular to the rod (Fig. 1) the incoming puck stops after the collision. In an impact along the axis of the rod onto one of the pucks (Fig. 2) the incoming puck rebounds in the opposite direction with speed $v/5$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2026-2-1-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 1» = Fig. 1]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2026-2-1-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 2» = Fig. 2]

Find the ratio $n$ of the mass of a dumbbell puck to the mass of the incoming puck, and the coefficient of restitution $e$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Oscillations of a piston
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Oscillations of a piston

A vertical cylinder under a piston of mass $m$, which can move along its axis without friction, contains $\nu$ moles of an ideal gas. The pressure and temperature of the surrounding air are $P_0$ and $T_0$, the cross-sectional area of the cylinder is $S$. The specific heat capacity of the gas at constant volume is $c_V$. The heat capacity of the cylinder and the piston may be neglected. Initially the system is in equilibrium, and the gas temperature is $T_0$.

Assuming the processes in the gas to be quasi-static, determine the angular frequency of small free oscillations of the piston in two cases: when the gas temperature is kept constant ($\Omega_T$) and when the cylinder is completely thermally insulated ($\Omega_S$).

Now let the cylinder not be insulated. The heat transfer power due to heat exchange between the gas under the piston and the surrounding air is given by the expression:

$$N=\beta(T-T_0),$$

where $T$ is the gas temperature and $\beta$ is a known coefficient. Under a periodic external force the piston performs small forced oscillations according to the law:

$$y(t)=h\sin(\Omega t),$$

where $y$ is the displacement of the piston from the equilibrium position, and the axis $OY$ is directed upward. Some time after the force begins to act, small harmonic oscillations of the temperature difference $\Delta T=T-T_0$ are established. Determine the amplitude of these oscillations and the phase difference between the oscillations of the temperature difference and the vertical coordinate of the piston.

problems.title: Problem 3: Construction
problems.problem:
Problem 3: Construction

A thin ideal converging lens and a plane mirror (see Fig. 3) are placed parallel to each other at a distance equal to the focal length $f$ of the lens. An ideal lens is a thin lens in which any rays, including those at large angles to the optical axis, are refracted as paraxial ones.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2026-2-3-fig1.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 3» = Fig. 3]

A luminous point is at a distance $a$ from the lens ($f\leqslant a\leqslant 2f$) on the side opposite to the mirror. At what distance from the lens is its image in this system?

Fig. 4 shows the image of an object in the form of a circle (the plane of the circle is perpendicular to the plane of the mirror) obtained in this optical system. It is known that the image coincides with the object; the points $L$ and $M$ marked in Fig. 4 lie on the lens and on the mirror respectively.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/moscow-2026-2-3-fig2.png
[Labels in the figure: «Рис. 4» = Fig. 4]

Using a compass and a straightedge, construct the optical centre and the foci of the lens on an additional sheet with an enlarged Fig. 4. Give a justification of your construction (describing the algorithm of standard geometric constructions is not required). The additional sheet with the construction must be handed in together with the work.

problems.title: Problem 4: Polyswitch
problems.problem:
Problem 4: Polyswitch

A fuse is a single-use protective element. Its modern reusable alternative is the self-resetting fuse (also known as a Polyswitch).

The device is based on a polymer material with conductive inclusions. When the critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{m}}$ is reached, a phase transition occurs in the material: the conducting paths are destroyed and the electrical resistance of the device increases sharply. When the material cools below $T_{\mathrm{m}}$, the structure of the conducting paths is restored and the resistance returns to its initial low value.

The behaviour of a certain self-resetting fuse is proposed to be described by the following simplified model. At temperatures below the critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{m}}=120\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ its resistance is constant and equal to $R_1=1\ \Omega$. At $T_{\mathrm{m}}$ it jumps to $R_2=10\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$ and does not change on further heating. At the very point of the phase transition (at $T=T_{\mathrm{m}}$) the resistance can take any intermediate values in the range from $1\ \Omega$ to $10\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$.

Assume that the heat transfer power from the fuse to the environment is described by the relation

$$P=\alpha(T-T_0),$$

where $\alpha=10\ \mathrm{mW/^\circ C}$ is the heat transfer coefficient, $T_0=20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is the ambient temperature, and $T$ is the temperature of the fuse.

Draw the static current–voltage characteristic (I–V curve) of the fuse, assuming that at every point of the I–V curve it is in a steady thermal regime.

Let the fuse be connected to an ideal source with EMF $\mathcal{E}=10\ \mathrm{V}$ in series with a rheostat, whose resistance can vary from $0$ to $50\ \Omega$, and an inductor of inductance $L$. Assume that the inductance of the inductor is so large that the thermal balance in the fuse is established much faster than the current changes. This allows the state of the fuse to be described by its static I–V curve at any moment of time.

How many operating points can in theory be realised in the circuit for different values of the rheostat resistance? Which of these points are stable with respect to fluctuations of the current in the circuit?

An operating point is considered stable in current if, for a small deviation of the current from its value at the operating point, the self-induction EMF arising in the inductor tends to return the circuit to the initial state.

Now consider a real circuit. The fuse is connected through a switch in series with a resistor $R$ to two series-connected 3R12 batteries (the EMF of each is $\mathcal{E}=4.5\ \mathrm{V}$, the internal resistance is $r=1\ \Omega$). What current will be established in the circuit after the switch is closed, if $R=7\ \Omega$?

Describe qualitatively the processes occurring in the circuit after the switch is closed if the resistance of the resistor is $R=2\ \Omega$. Take into account that in this case the current may change so fast that the temperature of the fuse will not have time to adjust to the current value of the power.

problems.title: Problem 5: Magnet falling in a tube
problems.problem:
Problem 5: Magnet falling in a tube

While solving this problem, some or all of the formulas given below may turn out to be useful (or may not).

Equations for an axisymmetric magnetic field in vacuum in cylindrical coordinates:

$$\frac{1}{r}\cdot\frac{\partial(rB_r)}{\partial r}+\frac{\partial B_z}{\partial z}=0\qquad\frac{\partial B_r}{\partial z}-\frac{\partial B_z}{\partial r}=0$$

The relation between the radial component $B_r$ of an axisymmetric field and the magnetic flux $\Phi(z)$ through a disc of radius $R$ whose centre lies on the axis $OZ$ at the point with coordinate $z$ and whose plane is perpendicular to this axis:

$$B_r(R,z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi R}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi}{\mathrm{d}z}.$$

The axial and radial components of the field of a magnetic dipole with moment $m$ (the moment is directed along the axis $OZ$):

$$B_z(z,r)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{m\,(2z^2-r^2)}{(z^2+r^2)^{5/2}},\qquad B_r(z,r)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{3mzr}{(z^2+r^2)^{5/2}}.$$

The field at the centre of the base of a cylindrical permanent magnet (base radius $a$, height $h$, magnetic moment $m$):

$$B_0=\frac{\mu_0 m}{2\pi a^2\sqrt{a^2+h^2}}.$$

The values of some improper integrals:

$$\int_0^\infty\frac{x^2\,\mathrm{d}x}{(x^2+a^2)^4}=\frac{\pi}{32a^5},\qquad\int_0^\infty\frac{x^2\,\mathrm{d}x}{(x^2+a^2)^5}=\frac{5\pi}{256a^7}$$

Consider a thin ring of radius $R$ made of wire of cross-section $S$ ($S\ll R^2$). The conductivity of the ring material (the reciprocal of the resistivity) $\sigma=\frac{1}{\rho}$ is known. The ring moves with constant speed $v$ along the axis $OZ$, which coincides with the axis of symmetry of the magnetic field and of the ring itself. Considering the functions $B_z(z,r)$ and $B_r(z,r)$, which give the axial and radial components of the magnetic induction, as known, find the force acting on the ring at the point with coordinate $z$.

A small magnet with moment $m$ directed along the axis $OZ$ is fixed at the origin. A very long thin-walled tube of radius $R$ and wall thickness $d$ ($d\ll R$) moves along the same axis. The axis of the tube coincides with the axis $OZ$, and its speed $v$ is constant. The tube material has conductivity $\sigma$. Determine the force of interaction between the tube and the magnet.

A coaxial cylindrical neodymium magnet (base radius $a=0.5\ \mathrm{cm}$, height $h=2a$) falls in a vertical copper tube ($R=1\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d=1\ \mathrm{mm}$). Some time after the fall begins, the speed of the magnet becomes constant. Determine this steady speed, assuming that the field outside the magnet coincides with the field of a point dipole located at its centre and having the same magnetic moment. Air resistance may be neglected.

The density of the magnet material is $\rho_{\mathrm{m}}=7.4\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$, the conductivity of copper is $\sigma=5.8\cdot10^{7}\ (\Omega\cdot\mathrm{m})^{-1}$. The magnet creates a field $B_0=1\ \mathrm{T}$ at the centre of its base. The free-fall acceleration is $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

problems.title: Problem 1: Kinematic construction
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Kinematic construction

A flat disc rotates about its axis of symmetry, fixed vertically. The points $A$ and $B$ belong to this disc. Fig. 1 shows the acceleration vector of point $A$ and the velocity vector of point $B$. It is known that the acceleration vector of point $B$ lies on the line shown dashed in Fig. 1.
